\title{}

\begin{abstract}
Row polymorphism and GADTs make opposite demands on the same variable:
unification solves an equation globally; GADT refinement keeps it
branch-local. No published type system refines a row variable by a
branch-local GADT equation; the one widely used language that ships both
documents the interaction as ``not well specified'' and restricted its
first GADT implementation. We present λρG, a calculus of branch-local
row refinement: a scoped equation store \emph{captures}, rather than
solves, the equations a match puts on rigid variables, and a two-tier
result rule, \textbf{directed by the kind of the equation}, lets a
\emph{type} equation coerce at a branch result while a \emph{row}
equation never escapes --- its discharge would move the row's domain out
of the branch. The discipline yields an operation-level answer:
selection is licensed exactly by the heads of the branch's equations;
scoped-label update is domain-preserving, hence sound by construction;
insertion, the shape-changing dual, is rejected --- a deliberate
position on Rémy's extension dial, not a discovery. A measured
principality boundary carries an inversion: the witness encoding
\emph{infers} where the native refinement is \emph{checkable, not
inferable}. An Elm-family checker implements it: the pre-existing corpus
compiles byte-identically against a committed manifest, 154 regression
checks pass, and an external state machine translated from an OCaml
thread now has its impossible match arms refuted at compile time. An
adversarial hunt across three passes found five unsound accepts --- two
in the first escape check, two in the shipping checks, one in the
coercion surface --- all fixed and pinned by gate fixtures, the two
escape-check accepts additionally mechanized as theorems, the last
closed by a class-level repair of the equation lifecycle; and the
compiler's own effect interpreter checks 16 of 20 branches honestly, the
four holdouts named and decomposed by kind of lie. Ninety Lean theorems
(three explicit axioms) mechanize the row-rewrite commutation under
duplicate labels --- one of them corrects our own specification --- the
escape domain rule, the update theorem, and the typing judgment's
row-specific obligations (the store discipline and record-operation
preservation), with the unifier abstracted as a parameter. We do not
prove general soundness: progress and preservation are argued.
\end{abstract}

\maketitle

Rows under Refinement: Branch-Local GADT Equations for Extensible
Records

\section{1 Introduction}\label{introduction}

Extensible records with row polymorphism and GADTs with local type
refinement are each well understood. Row polymorphism {[}Rémy 1994;
Gaster \& Jones 1996; Leijen 2005{]} gives records open types ---
\texttt{\{\ n\ :\ Int\ \textbar{}\ ρ\ \}} is a record with an \texttt{n}
field and an arbitrary tail ρ --- and unification over row variables
preserves principal types. GADTs give pattern matches that \emph{refine}
type variables branch-locally: matching \texttt{Int\allowbreak{}Lit\ :\ Expr\ Int}
inside \texttt{eval\ :\ Expr\ a\ →\ a} learns \texttt{a\ ≐\ Int} for
that branch alone. The two mechanisms make opposite demands on the same
object. Row unification wants a type variable to be \emph{solvable}: an
equation such as
\texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ x\ :\ Int\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}} is
written back into a single global substitution. GADT refinement wants an
equation to be \emph{local}: two branches of one match may learn
conflicting facts about one variable, so no global substitution can hold
them both. Every GADT-inference framework resolves this by making
refined variables rigid --- untouchable by the solver {[}Vytiniotis et
al.~2011; Pottier \& Régis-Gianas 2006{]} --- and every row system
resolves it by never putting a row variable under an equation at all.
The interaction is genuinely unoccupied: no published type system
refines a \emph{row variable} by a branch-local GADT equation, and no
published system therefore says which record operations remain typable
when such an equation is active.

The gap is documented, not merely empty. OCaml ships all three features
--- GADTs, row-polymorphic objects and polymorphic variants, and the
locally abstract type prefix \texttt{type\ a.} --- and its maintainers
describe the interaction precisely. OCaml's first GADT implementation
\emph{restricted} the combination outright: ``we had to restrict the use
of object types and polymorphic variants in combination with GADTs, to
prevent local equations from breaking the invariant that the same row
variable may only appear in two record types that are equal''
{[}Garrigue \& Rémy 2012{]}. Its residue is still felt as an
undocumented idiom with empirical failure modes: ``the interaction of
row variables and GADTs is not well specified. Thus it is common to hit
hard to understand behaviour, and nothing is guaranteed beyond the fact
that the currently implemented interaction is safe'' {[}octachron, OCaml
maintainer, Jan 2024{]}. Pattern matching on a polymorphic variant
blocks refinement entirely (``GADT equations cannot narrow a polymorphic
variant constraint'' {[}octachron 2024{]}; ocaml/\allowbreak{}ocaml \#5724 records an
earlier, stronger 4.00-era restriction --- no type propagation in any
match containing a poly-variant pattern --- lifted in 4.01 {[}Garrigue,
rev 13221; 4.01 Changes{]}), and the recommended workaround restructures
the program so that no single row variable is ever refined: model each
field as its own one-field object type, which is a manual
membership-witness encoding. Practitioners reach for witness encodings
by necessity. The one system that met the interaction treated the
conflict as unsoundness and legislated around it; the dominant
GADT-inference framework cannot even state it --- OutsideIn(X)'s type
grammar
\texttt{τ\ ::=\ tv\ \textbar{}\ Int\ \textbar{}\ Bool\ \textbar{}\ {[}τ{]}\ \textbar{}\ T\ τ}
has no record type, no row variable, and no presence {[}Vytiniotis et
al.~2011{]}.

\textbf{The contrast this paper turns on: where GADT inference decides
solvability by \emph{scope} --- a touchable/\allowbreak{}untouchable variable set ---
λρG decides discharge by the \emph{kind} of the equation.} A type
equation coerces at a branch result; a row equation never escapes,
because it carries a \emph{domain} that OutsideIn(X)'s type grammar has
no room for.

\subsection{1.1 The motivating example}\label{the-motivating-example}

The smallest program that needs all three features --- rows, GADT
refinement, and locally abstract types --- is a type-indexed
row-membership witness (Figure 1). \texttt{Has\ l\ t\ ρ} is a GADT
proving that the row ρ carries a field \texttt{l\ :\ t}; \texttt{select}
reads that field through the witness; \texttt{setx} replaces it.

{\footnotesize\begin{verbatim}
type Has l t rho
    = Here : Has l t { l : t | rho }
    | There : Has l t rho -> Has l t { k : s | rho }


select : type rho l t. { rho | l : t } -> Has l t rho -> t
select r h =
    case h of
        Here ->
            r.l

        There rest ->
            select r rest

setx : type rho l t. { rho | l : t } -> Has l t rho -> t -> { rho | l : t }
setx r h v =
    case h of
        Here ->
            { r | l = v }

        There rest ->
            setx r rest v
\end{verbatim}}

\textbf{Figure 1.} The central example --- the \texttt{Has} witness and
\texttt{select}, verbatim from gate fixture
\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}fixtures/\allowbreak{}rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}select.\allowbreak{}elm} (lines 8--20), and
\texttt{setx}, verbatim from
\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}fixtures/\allowbreak{}rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}setx.\allowbreak{}elm} (lines 13--20; the
\texttt{Has} block is identical in both fixtures); both fixtures compile
clean.

Each of the three features is forced:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Rows.} \texttt{\{\ rho\ \textbar{}\ l\ :\ t\ \}} is an open
  record; the function must work for every tail ρ, so the record's type
  \emph{is} a row variable.
\item
  \textbf{GADT refinement.} Matching \texttt{Here} learns the equation
  \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ l\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ₁\ \}} --- which is exactly
  what makes \texttt{r.\allowbreak{}l} well-typed --- and matching \texttt{There}
  learns \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ k\ :\ s\ \textbar{}\ ρ₂\ \}} for labels
  \texttt{k\ ≠\ l}. The readable field set must \emph{grow inside a
  branch} and shrink back at its end.
\item
  \textbf{Locally abstract types.} The two branches impose
  \emph{conflicting global} substitutions on ρ. A single substitution
  cannot hold \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ l\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ₁\ \}} and
  \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ k\ :\ s\ \textbar{}\ ρ₂\ \}} for distinct
  \texttt{l}, \texttt{k}. Only a rigid ρ --- abstract within the body,
  as the \texttt{type\ rho\ l\ t.} prefix declares --- keeps each
  branch's equation local to that branch.
\end{itemize}

Without locally-abstract rigidity the two branches conflict and
\texttt{select} has no type --- this is the necessity of the third
feature. (The \emph{measured} rejection is the \textbf{signatureless}
form, gate fixture \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}l3ii}, which reports
\texttt{cannot\ unify\ \{k:a\textbar{}\ b\}\ with\ \{\textbar{}\ a\}};
note it measures signaturelessness wholesale rather than a flexible ρ in
isolation, since that fixture carries no signature at all.) Without
refinement capture the \texttt{Here} branch's equation has nowhere to
live; without rows the record cannot stay open.

\subsection{1.2 The design in one
paragraph}\label{the-design-in-one-paragraph}

λρG (Section 2) is a calculus of \textbf{branch-local row refinement}. A
scoped equation store Δ accompanies the judgment
\texttt{Γ\ ;\ Δ\ ;\ R\ ⊢\ e\ :\ t}, where R is the set of rigid (skolem)
variables. At a pattern match, the store is \emph{snapshotted}; the
pattern-vs-scrutinee unification runs in \emph{branch mode}, where a
unification that would bind a rigid variable is \textbf{captured} as an
equation in Δ rather than solved --- the global substitution θ gains
nothing; at branch end the store is \emph{truncated} to the snapshot.
Inside a branch, the equations \emph{license} operations: selection
\texttt{r.\allowbreak{}l} is licensed exactly when some equation on ρ exposes
\texttt{l} at its head; update \texttt{\{\ r\ \textbar{}\ l\ =\ v\ \}}
is licensed the same way and, crucially, is \textbf{domain-preserving}
--- scoped-label update replaces the first occurrence of \texttt{l} and
never extends the row --- so the branch result is well-typed at the
abstract ρ with \emph{no discharge at all}. At the branch result, a
\textbf{two-tier} rule decides what may leave the branch: a \emph{type}
equation (\texttt{a\ ≐\ Int}) is discharged by a one-way coercion of the
re-check --- the canonical GADT evaluator type-checks --- but a
\emph{row} equation
(\texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ l\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}}) never
discharges, because that would move the row's \emph{domain} out of the
branch; its escape is an error. Insertion, the shape-changing dual of
update, never consults the store and is rejected under an active
equation.

\subsection{1.3 The heterogeneous
container}\label{the-heterogeneous-container}

The same discipline unlocks type witnesses --- the encoding
practitioners use to recover an element type a container does not
mention.
\texttt{type\ Witness\ a\ =\ WInt\ :\ Witness\ Int\ \textbar{}\ WString\ :\ Witness\ String},
an existential wrapper
\texttt{Some\ :\ Witness\ a\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ a\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ Any},
and a fold over a list
\texttt{{[}Some\ WInt\ 3,\ Some\ WString\ "hi"{]}} all type-check (gate
fixture \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}het}, run \texttt{"hi3"}): the existential
\texttt{a} bound by the \texttt{Some} pattern is instantiated
\emph{rigid} (the ``existentials are skolems'' rule every GADT system
needs; before it, the \texttt{a} was a flexible unification variable, a
nested match bound it globally, and the sibling \texttt{WString} branch
conflicted --- two independently measured failures), and each nested
branch captures \texttt{a\ ≐\ Int} /\allowbreak{} \texttt{a\ ≐\ String} locally,
discharging at the use of the payload. This is the feature the witness
program generalizes: the \emph{witness encoding} of row membership is
what OCaml's own workaround constructs by hand, and the calculus that
makes \texttt{Has} typable also makes the hand encoding unnecessary.

\subsection{1.4 An external program, not a self-referential
one}\label{an-external-program-not-a-self-referential-one}

The strongest objection to a paper like this is that its only non-toy
evidence is the authors' own compiler. We answer with a program written
by someone else. A discuss.ocaml.org thread (``Unable to refute
impossible GADT pattern with polymorphic variants'', t/\allowbreak{}13718) models a
door state machine: states as types, transitions as a GADT-witnessed
relation, and a fold over the chain of events --- and there the author
hits the wall this paper characterizes, on all three sides: illegal
construction is rejected, but the \emph{impossible arms} of the chain
match cannot be refuted, and the recommended fix is the per-field-object
workaround. We retrieved and read the thread in full and translated the
program into the reference implementation --- the surface of λρG (the
example lives at \texttt{examples/\allowbreak{}research/\allowbreak{}fsm/\allowbreak{}door.\allowbreak{}elm}; gate fixtures
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}fsm}, \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}fsm\_\allowbreak{}bad},
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}fsm\_\allowbreak{}narrow}, \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}fsm\_\allowbreak{}nested},
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}fsm\_\allowbreak{}nested\_\allowbreak{}bad} pin its behaviour).

States are rows --- \texttt{Locked\ =\ \{\}},
\texttt{Closed\ =\ \{\ closed\ :\ Int\ \}},
\texttt{Open\ =\ \{\ open\ :\ Int\ \}},
\texttt{Broken\ =\ \{\ broken\ :\ String\ \}}. A state is its marker
plus a shared counter \texttt{n\ :\ Int}; the alias
\texttt{State\ marker\ =\ \{\ marker\ \textbar{}\ n\ :\ Int\ \}} names
that row extension:

{\normalsize\begin{verbatim}
type alias State marker =
    { marker | n : Int }

type Event from to
    = Unlock : Event {} { closed : Int }
    | Open   : Event { closed : Int } { open : Int }
    | Close  : Event { open : Int } { closed : Int }
    | Lock   : Event { closed : Int } {}
    | Jiggle : Event { closed : Int } { closed : Int }
    | Break  : Event { open : Int } { broken : String }
    | Reset  : Event { broken : String } {}

readFrom : type from to. State from -> Event from to -> String
readFrom rec ev =
    case ev of
        Unlock -> "locked#" ++ String.fromInt rec.n
        Open   -> "closed:" ++ String.fromInt rec.closed
        Close  -> "open:"   ++ String.fromInt rec.open
        ...
\end{verbatim}}

Where OCaml's equations ``cannot narrow a polymorphic variant
constraint'', the reference implementation's narrowing is direct and
\emph{per-branch}: in the \texttt{Open} branch the from-row is refined
to \texttt{\{\ closed\ :\ Int\ \}} and \texttt{rec.\allowbreak{}closed} is well-typed
\emph{only there} --- in the \texttt{Close} branch (from-row
\texttt{\{\ open\ :\ Int\ \}}) the read \texttt{rec.\allowbreak{}broken} is rejected
with
\texttt{type\ variable\ a\ is\ rigid\ (from\ the\ signature)\ and\ cannot\ be\ unified\ with\ \{broken:a\textbar{}\ b\}}
(gate fixture \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}fsm\_\allowbreak{}narrow}, re-measured), while the
\emph{same field} is legal in the \texttt{Reset} branch (from-row
\texttt{\{\ broken\ :\ String\ \}}): the rejection is per-branch, not
per-field. No per-field restructuring is needed: the states \emph{are}
rows, and the refinement is the mechanism, not the workaround.

The thread's \emph{headline} wall is refutation, and that too is
answered. The source author could not get OCaml to refute the impossible
arms of the chain match (its \texttt{-\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ .} mechanism). The
reference implementation now checks \emph{exhaustiveness} --- a match
omitting a possible arm is a compile error, not a runtime raise (fixture
\texttt{adtgaps}) --- and \emph{refutes} impossible arms under the
branch equations:
\texttt{describe\allowbreak{}Broken\ :\ Step\ \{\ broken\ :\ String\ \}\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ String}
matching only \texttt{Then\ prev\ Break} compiles clean, because
\texttt{Start\ :\ Step\ \{\}} and every other event are impossible at
that index (fixture \texttt{refutpos}; the negative \texttt{refutneg}
pins that a \emph{possible} arm, \texttt{HNil} at an open
\texttt{HList\ ρ}, is not refuted and must still be matched). Refutation
has a stated condition: it fires only where the scrutinee's index is
\emph{concrete or binder-rigid}; a bare flexible index is never
concretized to refute a sibling (fixture \texttt{refutbare} --- a
partial \texttt{f\ :\ Tag\ a\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ Int} matching only one
arm correctly errors \texttt{non-\allowbreak{}exhaustive\ case:\ missing\ B}).

The translation is honest about three boundaries, stated here rather
than hidden. (i) The transition GADT is \emph{row-inert}:
\texttt{Event}'s indices are ordinary type parameters, so the row
refinement exercised is on the \emph{record argument's} row variable ---
the honest claim is ``an external FSM translated to rows where per-state
field reads use branch-local row refinement'', not ``the FSM expressed
directly''. (ii) A reducer whose \emph{result} is a record at the
refined row is rejected by the escape rule --- including the
state-\emph{preserving} \texttt{Jiggle} update, because the refined
variable there is the result index; the FSM keeps its state type-level,
as the OCaml original does. (iii) The membership-witness reducer
\texttt{read} is definable but not \emph{callable} at a concrete witness
(\texttt{read\ Here\ \{\ n\ =\ 1,\ closed\ =\ 2\ \}} errs
\texttt{cannot\ unify\ a\ with\ \{l:a\textbar{}\ b\}} --- a global
bare-row-variable gap in the implementation, outside branch mode); the
example keeps the witness as the shape \texttt{read\allowbreak{}From} reduces to, not
as a working reducer. The example demonstrates capability where it holds
and names the boundary where it does not.

\subsection{1.5 Why the cell stayed
empty}\label{why-the-cell-stayed-empty}

The empty cell is not an accident of oversight. Rows and GADTs were
adopted by disjoint language populations --- ML-family record calculi in
the early 1990s, GADT inference in the mid-2000s --- and the frameworks
that made GADT inference tractable (OutsideIn(X), stratified inference,
HMG(X)) were built on type grammars without rows. Where the two
populations met, rows were \emph{secondary}: in OCaml, objects and
polymorphic variants are not the primary record mechanism, so
restricting their interaction with GADTs costs little and the
per-field-object workaround is cheap. In a language where rows are the
primary record mechanism, the same restriction removes the core feature.
And the interaction is a \emph{kinding} problem as much as an equation
problem: three of the four implementation blockers we hit building the
reference implementation were kinding defects (Section 6) --- a calculus
that does not make row-variable kinding explicit cannot predict where a
real implementation breaks. Generic local-assumption frameworks could in
principle host this: HMG(X) is parameterised over a constraint domain X,
but no published instantiation of it targets a row/\allowbreak{}record theory, and
the two row-specific obligations our discipline needs (the
rewrite/\allowbreak{}equation commutation under scoped-label duplicates, and the
domain escape rule) do not come out of the generic frame for free
(Section 4).

\subsection{1.6 Contributions}\label{contributions}

This paper's claims are of three kinds --- \emph{mechanized}
(machine-checked in the Lean development), \emph{measured} (reproduced
by the reference implementation, with fixtures registered in a
regression gate), and \emph{argued} (stated with their mechanism, not
proved) --- and the text marks each. In outline:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{A discipline for an unoccupied cell, built on one principle.}
  λρG is the first designed account of what happens when a row variable
  sits under a branch-local GADT equation. The principle is a discharge
  rule \textbf{directed by the kind of the equation}: at a branch result
  a \emph{type} equation coerces, while a \emph{row} equation never
  discharges --- its discharge would move the row's domain out of the
  branch. The machinery is a scoped equation store that snapshots,
  captures would-be rigid bindings as equations, and truncates on branch
  exit (Sections 2--3). The program of Figure 1 type-checks under the
  discipline; its signatureless form is rejected --- the measured face
  of the rigidity requirement.
\item
  \textbf{An operation-level answer, with the positive row result
  mechanized.} Under an active refinement: selection is licensed exactly
  by the heads of the branch's equations (a field in no head is an error
  inside the branch); update is sound \emph{by construction}, because
  scoped-label update is domain-preserving and the branch result is
  well-typed at the abstract row with no discharge; insertion is
  rejected --- a deliberate position on a dial Rémy set to
  \emph{unconditional} and Gaster \& Jones to \emph{strict}, not a
  discovery (Section 3; mechanized: \texttt{update\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}preserving},
  \texttt{update\_\allowbreak{}reflexive\_\allowbreak{}domain},
  \texttt{update\_\allowbreak{}accepted\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}rho},
  \texttt{insertion\_\allowbreak{}rejected\_\allowbreak{}under\_\allowbreak{}refinement}).
\item
  \textbf{A measured principality boundary, and its inversion.}
  Principality is retained where every refinement's target is a
  branch-scoped existential --- the \emph{witness encoding infers} with
  no signature --- and lost exactly where two sibling branches refine
  one \emph{signature} row variable whose result mentions it: there the
  native form is \emph{checkable, not inferable}. The inversion is the
  result: the encoding does not merely model rows, it \textbf{moves the
  boundary to the other side} of the native form (Section 5, the L3
  measurement).
\item
  \textbf{Mechanized metatheory for the row obligations, validated by an
  adversarial hunt.} Ninety machine-checked Lean theorems (three
  explicit axiom parameters; clean build, zero \texttt{sorry}) cover the
  row-rewrite commutation under duplicate labels --- including the
  theorem that \emph{corrected our own specification}
  (\texttt{h1\_\allowbreak{}head\_\allowbreak{}only\_\allowbreak{}vs\_\allowbreak{}full}: the ``for every label'' form holds
  only in the rigid-tail regime) --- the escape rule as a \emph{domain}
  rule (exact for fresh labels, coarse for duplicates), the update
  theorems, and both escape counterexamples. An adversarial hunt across
  three passes found five \emph{real unsound accepts} --- the first
  escape check's let-laundering through let-generalization and its
  wildcard sibling leak, two in the shipping checks, and one in the
  coercion surface --- all fixed, all pinned by fixtures; the two
  escape-check accepts are additionally mechanized as theorems
  (\texttt{H2b\_\allowbreak{}no\_\allowbreak{}quantify\_\allowbreak{}refined\_\allowbreak{}tail},
  \texttt{H2b\_\allowbreak{}wildcard\_\allowbreak{}leak\_\allowbreak{}shape}), and the coercion-surface one is
  closed by a class-level repair of the equation lifecycle (Section
  6.2).
\item
  \textbf{A working reference implementation, measured against itself
  and an external program.} The discipline runs inside an Elm-family
  checker: the pre-existing corpus compiles \emph{byte-identically}
  after the change --- 149 artifacts with zero moved --- and the
  committed sha256 manifest holds 149 entries; the gate passes 154/\allowbreak{}154,
  and the compiler's own effect interpreter checks 16 of its 20 branches
  honestly (reproducible bisection script; the four holdouts named, one
  of them deliberate) --- \emph{(Section 6)}. The external program --- a
  state machine translated from an OCaml discussion thread --- reads
  per-state fields under branch-local refinement and has its impossible
  match arms \textbf{refuted at compile time}, the thread's headline
  wall answered under the rigidity guard of Section 1.4.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Scope, stated once.} We do not prove general soundness: progress
and preservation are argued, not proved. What the mechanization
\emph{does} prove are exactly the row-specific obligations the argued
soundness rests on --- the rewrite/\allowbreak{}equation commutation (H1), the update
domain theorem, the store discipline and escape rule of the typing
judgment (\texttt{tier\_\allowbreak{}R\_\allowbreak{}forces\_\allowbreak{}escape} and companions), and
record-operation preservation --- plus the escape counterexamples, all
with the unifier abstracted as a parameter (Section 4.1). A paper claim
we cannot trace to a theorem name, a fixture, or a measurement is cut
rather than hedged.

\subsection{1.7 The map of the paper}\label{the-map-of-the-paper}

Section 2 presents λρG: syntax with explicit row kinds, the two
unification modes, and the rule set. Section 3 gives the two-tier result
rule and the operation-level answer: which record operations survive an
active refinement. Section 4 states the metatheory --- mechanized,
argued, and refuted --- and the negative result that unrestricted global
row refinement is unsound. Section 5 locates the principality boundary
and its inversion. Section 6 reports the implementation, the measured
correspondence, and the adversarial hunt. Section 7 organizes related
work by the feature-pair map --- the organization itself is a
contribution, because it makes the empty cell visible. Section 8 states
limitations; Section 9 concludes.


\section{2 λρG: a calculus of branch-local row
refinement}\label{ux3bbux3c1g-a-calculus-of-branch-local-row-refinement}

This section presents the declarative calculus; the full rule set with
its implementation seats is the companion specification
(\texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}research/\allowbreak{}row-\allowbreak{}gadt-\allowbreak{}calculus.\allowbreak{}md}), and the mechanization of
its hard lemmas is Section 4. Here we give syntax, the judgment, the two
unification modes, the store discipline, and the rule inventory (Figures
2 and 3).

\subsection{2.1 Syntax and kinds}\label{syntax-and-kinds}

{\scriptsize\begin{verbatim}
k    ::=  Ty | Row                            kinds
x̂    ::=  (id, k, φ)                          variables: id, kind, flex marker
φ    ::=  none | number | comparable | appendable
t    ::=  a  |  T t⃗  |  t → t  |  (t⃗)  |  { r }        types
r    ::=  ε  |  ℓ : t | r  |  ρ                rows: fields in source order + tail
s    ::=  ∀ B; x̂⃗. t                           schemes with a bound subset B
\end{verbatim}}

\textbf{Figure 2.} Syntax and kinds --- kinds, variables with flex
markers, types and rows, and schemes with a bound subset. Source:
\texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}research/\allowbreak{}row-\allowbreak{}gadt-\allowbreak{}calculus.\allowbreak{}md} §1.1--1.4 (compressed).

Labels ℓ are surface strings (there are no type-level labels). Duplicate
labels are legal and retained; the \textbf{first occurrence} of a label
is the one selection, restriction, and update act on (Leijen's scoped
labels) --- this is definitional and load-bearing: the duplicate case is
exactly where the hard lemma bites (Section 4.2). Substitutions θ are
kinded and id-keyed; a \texttt{Row} variable's image is always a record
value (a row variable never maps to a bare type).

\textbf{Kinds are explicit, and the build proved they must be} (Section
6.1): three of the four implementation blockers were kinding defects.
Well-formedness keeps a \texttt{Row} variable only in tail position (by
construction: the row grammar's tail is \texttt{ε\ \textbar{}\ ρ}, never
a type variable).

Declarations carry per-constructor \textbf{annotated result types} ---
the GADT form:

{\footnotesize\begin{verbatim}
data Has (l : Ty) (t : Ty) (ρ : Row) where
  Here   : Has l t { l : t | ρ' }             -- ρ' a fresh per-ctor existential
  There  : Has l t ρ₀ -> Has l t { k : s | ρ₀ }
\end{verbatim}}

A constructor's scheme is \texttt{∀} its free variables; the variables
\emph{not free in its result} are its true existentials.

\subsection{2.2 The judgment and the
store}\label{the-judgment-and-the-store}

{\normalsize\begin{verbatim}
Γ ; Δ ; R ⊢ e : t
\end{verbatim}}

\textbf{Figure 2 (continued).} The judgment
\texttt{Γ\ ;\ Δ\ ;\ R\ ⊢\ e\ :\ t}. Source:
\texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}research/\allowbreak{}row-\allowbreak{}gadt-\allowbreak{}calculus.\allowbreak{}md} §2.1.

Γ types term variables (with schemes); \textbf{Δ is the equation store}
--- a most-recent-first list of equations \texttt{x̂\ ≐\ t} (either kind,
kind-matched); \textbf{R is the set of rigid variable ids} (skolems).
The \textbf{global substitution θ} --- the persistent state of inference
--- is deliberately \emph{separate}: equations in Δ are never solved
into θ while their target is rigid.

Rigidity has exactly three scoped origins: \textbf{signature-bound} (the
\texttt{type\ x̂⃗.} prefix, or a GADT-index position --- Section 6.3);
\textbf{constructor-existential} (a pattern's constructor quantifiers
not free in its result are skolems of that branch --- OutsideIn's
touchables, row-aware); and \textbf{index-lift} (a signature index free
in the scrutinee that a pattern's result equates to a structured type is
lifted rigid for the branch's duration). Everything else is flex.

\subsection{2.3 Unification's two modes}\label{unifications-two-modes}

\texttt{unify\_\allowbreak{}δ(θ,\ R;\ t₁\ ≐\ t₂)} with δ ∈ \{global, branch\} is
ordinary unification (decomposition, occurs check, scoped-label row
rewrite) plus one discipline: what happens when unification \emph{would
bind a rigid variable}.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{U-RIGID-BIND.} \texttt{a\ ≐\ t} with \texttt{a} rigid:
  \textbf{global} fails (\texttt{Rigid\allowbreak{}Var}); \textbf{branch}
  \emph{captures} the equation \texttt{a\ ≐\ t} into Δ and leaves
  \texttt{a} unbound.
\item
  \textbf{U-RIGID-BIND-R.} \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{r\}} with \texttt{ρ} rigid:
  same split --- with one exception, the \textbf{alias case}: if the row
  is a bare flex variable (\texttt{ρ\ ≐\ ρ\textquotesingle{}}, no
  fields), the flex variable is bound \emph{to}
  \texttt{\{\ ε\ \textbar{}\ ρ\ \}} in both modes, and nothing is
  captured. (The dual direction --- rigid bound to flex --- never
  arises: binding direction is always flex-gets-bound.)
\item
  \textbf{U-RIGID-EXTEND.} The row rewrite reaching a rigid tail it
  would extend: \textbf{global} fails; \textbf{branch} captures
  \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ ℓ\ :\ γ\ \textbar{}\ β\ \}} (fresh γ, β) and
  \emph{proceeds}, handing out the exposed field view --- the one
  branch-mode behaviour that continues with a derived fact rather than
  failing.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What a rigid row tail may be --- the inventory, stated once.} A
rigid ρ \textbf{may}: (a) be aliased \emph{by} a flex row variable; (b)
be \emph{locally known}, inside a branch, to have a shape
\texttt{\{\ ℓ\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}} --- a captured
equation that licenses selection/\allowbreak{}update discharge within that branch
only; (c) unify with itself. A rigid ρ \textbf{may never --- in any mode
--- be bound in θ}: not to a closed row, not to a fielded row, not to
another rigid variable outside branch mode, and no rewrite may extend it
outside branch mode. In branch mode a would-be binding is captured, and
\textbf{θ gains nothing}: this is the invariant that makes the exported
scheme honest.

\subsection{2.4 The rules}\label{the-rules}

The rule set --- compressed here; the full rules, verbatim from the
companion spec, are Figure 3:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{R-VAR} instantiates a scheme's quantifiers with fresh
  \emph{flex} variables of matching kind.
\item
  \textbf{R-TYPE} checks a signatured declaration's clauses against the
  declared scheme with the \texttt{type}-bound quantifiers rigid;
  unnamed quantifiers stay flexible, restored by the \textbf{too-general
  police} after the body (Section 6.3).
\item
  \textbf{R-APP} unifies function with argument \emph{globally}; on a
  rigid failure explained by Δ (\textbf{R-APP-DISCH}), the \emph{type}
  equation is applied one-way (zonked both sides, occurs-guarded) and
  the unification re-run. This is the variable-use discharge:
  \texttt{String.\allowbreak{}from\allowbreak{}Int\ x} with \texttt{x\ :\ a} under
  \texttt{a\ ≐\ Int} succeeds without binding \texttt{a}.
\item
  \textbf{R-SEL} selects: unify the record with
  \texttt{\{\ ℓ\ :\ a\ \textbar{}\ β\ \}}; on a rigid-tail failure
  explained by Δ (\textbf{R-SEL-DISCH}) --- some equation on ρ zonks to
  a row whose \emph{head} is ℓ --- the selection is licensed and returns
  the equation's exposed type. \textbf{An equation whose head label
  differs from ℓ licenses nothing}: the readable field set inside a
  refining branch grows exactly by the heads of the branch's equations
  (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}absentfield}).
\item
  \textbf{R-UPD} updates: restrict the first occurrence of ℓ (requiring
  it present) and re-prepend; when the label is present only through a
  refinement (\textbf{R-UPD-DISCH}), the same discharge licenses it and
  the result is the discharged shape re-prepended. \textbf{Nothing is
  bound}: the equation is read, never consumed.
\item
  \textbf{R-UPD-INS (rejection).} Insertion
  \texttt{\{\ e\ \textbar{}\ ℓ\ ←\ v\ \}} --- which may extend or shadow
  --- \emph{never} consults the store; if the base's row tail is refined
  by this branch, the form is rejected outright (``insertion under rigid
  row refinement'').
\item
  \textbf{R-RESTR} restricts (\texttt{\{\ e\ −\ ℓ\ \}}):
  first-occurrence removal, no store consultation.
\item
  \textbf{R-CASE} is the discipline's heart: \textbf{snapshot Δ; unify
  pattern-vs-scrutinee in branch mode (capture); infer the body under Δ
  ∪ Δᵢ and the branch's lifted rigid set; check the body result
  (R-RESULT); truncate Δ to the snapshot.} Truncation is by construction
  exact --- restore assigns the snapshot prefix --- so nesting is safe
  at any depth. Two \emph{memories} survive into the clause: the refined
  targets (every variable a branch of this clause refined) and the
  refined tail pairs (each captured row equation's head and tail) ---
  they are what the result check enforces (R-RESULT), not a channel by
  which equations leak.
\item
  \textbf{R-RESULT} is the two-tier rule --- Section 3.1.
\item
  \textbf{R-EXISTS} instantiates a pattern's constructor scheme with its
  true existentials rigid (branch-scoped); non-GADT constructors have
  every quantifier free in the result, so ordinary ADT patterns are
  unaffected, and flex-marked quantifiers are never rigidified (this is
  what keeps a \texttt{Dict\ k\ v} pattern from skolemizing \texttt{k}
  --- the prelude stays green).
\item
  \textbf{R-LET} generalizes the free variables of the bound type not
  free in the environment --- with the refined-tail exclusion that
  closes the let-laundering hole (Section 4.4).
\end{itemize}

The implementation's two-pass declaration-directed \emph{retry} is an
artifact for corpus byte-identity (Section 6.5); \textbf{the declarative
calculus has only the declaration-directed rule}.

{\tiny\begin{verbatim}
──────────────────────── R-VAR
Γ(x) = s
─────────────────────────────
Γ ; Δ ; R ⊢ x : ⟦s⟧

───────────────────────────────────────────── R-TYPE (clause checking)
Γ(f) = ∀ B; qⱼ. t    B = {x̂₁…x̂ₙ}   (the `type`-prefixed names)
instantiatePartial: qⱼ ↦ fresh q̂ⱼ;  q̂ⱼ rigid ⟺ qⱼ ∈ B ∧ flex(qⱼ) = none
Γ ; Δ ; R ∪ {q̂ⱼ | qⱼ ∈ B} ⊢ clauses of f against t[qⱼ := q̂ⱼ]

\section{3 The two-tier result rule and the operation-level
answer}\label{the-two-tier-result-rule-and-the-operation-level-answer}

\subsection{3.1 The two-tier result rule and the operation
inventory}\label{the-two-tier-result-rule-and-the-operation-inventory}

At each branch's result, the body type \texttt{t\_\allowbreak{}b} is unified with the
expected \texttt{t\_\allowbreak{}r}. On a rigid failure the decision is two-tier ---
the asymmetry is the paper's central design claim:

\textbf{Tier-T (type equations discharge).} If \texttt{a\ ≐\ τ} is in Δ
with \texttt{a\ :\ Ty} and τ not a record type (occurs-guarded), the
branch result is re-checked with \texttt{a} one-way replaced by τ on
\emph{both} sides --- a single pass, never a bind. The equation still
dies at branch end. This is the standard GADT coercion: a branch knowing
\texttt{a\ ≐\ Int} may return an \texttt{Int} \emph{at} type \texttt{a},
so the canonical three-branch evaluator type-checks
(\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}eval}), and a wrong body --- a \texttt{String} where
the equation says \texttt{Int} --- still fails the re-check
(\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}evalbad}).

\textbf{Tier-R (row equations never discharge).} A row equation
\texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{r\}} never discharges at a result. The reason is
\emph{domains}: discharging it would identify the abstract row with one
particular field set, moving a domain change out of the branch --- the
exported scheme would promise a domain the signature does not. Its rigid
failure surfaces as the explicit \emph{escaping-row-equation} error.

The full decision procedure at a branch result, in order (Figure 4):

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Unify (both sides zonked first).
\item
  On success, three gates before acceptance, in order: the
  \textbf{tail-escape check} --- did this unification newly identify a
  refined tail with its head? (\texttt{drop\allowbreak{}Introduced}: the drop shape)
  → reject; the \textbf{flex→rigid alias gate} --- did it alias a
  refined target? (\texttt{refined\allowbreak{}Target\allowbreak{}Aliased\allowbreak{}By}) → reject; the
  \textbf{branch-end occurs check} --- does a pending \texttt{KType}
  equation's body now contain its target? (\texttt{pending\allowbreak{}Type\allowbreak{}Occurs}) →
  reject (\emph{infinite type}). All three pass → done.
\item
  On rigid failure: does the presented type \emph{rebuild} the head's
  refinement (unifies with the equation body, head not free in it)? →
  \textbf{accept without binding} (\texttt{rebuild\allowbreak{}Matches}).
\item
  Else, is there a usable \emph{type} equation? → Tier-T discharge.
\item
  Else, is the rigid variable this branch's constructor existential? →
  reject (\emph{escaping existential}).
\item
  Else, does any equation explain it? → reject (\emph{escaping row
  equation}).
\item
  Else: the historical rigid error.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Figure 4.} The branch-result decision procedure. Source:
\texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}research/\allowbreak{}row-\allowbreak{}gadt-\allowbreak{}calculus.\allowbreak{}md} §2.7 and the code ---
\texttt{unify\allowbreak{}Result\allowbreak{}M} (\texttt{elm-\allowbreak{}compiler/\allowbreak{}src/\allowbreak{}Type/\allowbreak{}Infer.\allowbreak{}elm:1498}):
unify first (\texttt{:1509}), then on success the three gates
\texttt{drop\allowbreak{}Introduced} (\texttt{:1511}),
\texttt{refined\allowbreak{}Target\allowbreak{}Aliased\allowbreak{}By} (\texttt{:1515}),

\texttt{rebuild\allowbreak{}Matches} (\texttt{:1534}) and the Tier-T discharge

\texttt{drop\allowbreak{}Introduced} (\texttt{:1842}), \texttt{rebuild\allowbreak{}Matches}
(\texttt{:1879}), \texttt{refined\allowbreak{}Target\allowbreak{}Aliased\allowbreak{}By} (\texttt{:1709}).

\textbf{The operation-level answer.} The rules decide, for each record
operation, whether it survives an active refinement
\texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ ℓ\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}} on the
base's tail:

{
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
operation
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright

\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright

\end{minipage} \\

\endlastfoot
select ℓ (the equation's head) & \textbf{licensed} & R-SEL-DISCH reads
the equation's exposed type \\
select m ∉ equation heads & \textbf{rejected} & no equation exposes m
(\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}absentfield}) \\
update ℓ = v & \textbf{licensed, no discharge needed} & update is
domain-preserving --- Section 3.2 \\
insert ℓ ← v & \textbf{rejected} & insertion is shape-changing;
R-UPD-INS never consults Δ \\
\end{longtable}
}

Selection is \emph{licensed exactly by the heads of the branch's
equations}; update is sound \emph{by construction}; insertion is the
shape-changing dual, rejected \emph{conditionally} --- a deliberate
position on the extension dial, not a discovery (Section 3.3).

\subsection{3.2 Update is safe by
construction}\label{update-is-safe-by-construction}

Scoped-label update replaces the \textbf{first occurrence} of ℓ and
requires it present; it never extends the row. So under the refinement
\texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ ℓ\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}}:

{\footnotesize\begin{verbatim}
dom({ ℓ : t_v | ρ' })  =  dom({ ℓ : t | ρ' })  =  dom(ρ)   under the equation
\end{verbatim}}

The branch may return the updated record \emph{at the abstract row}
\texttt{\{\ ρ\ \}} --- the domains are equal, no equation is consumed,
nothing escapes. Update needs no discharge rule at all: its
compatibility falls out of its semantics, not out of the type system.
The dual makes the claim non-vacuous: insertion \emph{can} change the
domain, which is exactly why it may never consult the store. Both
directions are mechanized (\texttt{update\_\allowbreak{}reflexive\_\allowbreak{}domain},
\texttt{update\_\allowbreak{}accepted\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}rho},
\texttt{insertion\_\allowbreak{}rejected\_\allowbreak{}under\_\allowbreak{}refinement}; Section 4.5).

\subsection{3.3 Positioning the insertion trade and the update
lineage}\label{positioning-the-insertion-trade-and-the-update-lineage}

Insertion is typable in the rows-only world --- this paper's rejection
exists \emph{only relative to an active branch equation}, and the dial
has published settings. \textbf{Rémy 1994} types unrestricted field
extension \emph{unconditionally}:
\texttt{new\_\allowbreak{}a\ :\ Π(a:φ;\$)\ →\ α\ →\ Π(a:pre(α);\$)}, no lacks
predicate, no presence check; his \texttt{with} never requires the field
present and imposes ``no constraint between the types of the old and the
new values''. \textbf{Gaster \& Jones 1996} dial the same operation to
\emph{strict}:
\texttt{(l\ =\textbar{})\ ::\ (r\textbackslash{}l)\ ⇒\ …}, extension
under a lacks predicate. \textbf{CORELINKS} types insert by
\emph{quantifying presence} over the needed row. Our rule is the fourth
position --- \emph{conditional}: unrestricted outside refinement,
rejected under an active equation --- and the first account of
\emph{why} the condition exists: a discharged insertion is a domain
change escaping its branch. We give up Rémy's expressiveness exactly
where it would break refinement soundness.

Record update has the same lineage, and the contrast is the direction
that matters. Rémy's update is extension (shadowing; the domain may
grow); Gaster \& Jones' is restrict-then-extend under lacks; the Links
system derives remove-then-extend --- attested in the CORELINKS aside,
not in Links' own FMCO'06 paper, which defines no record update. Ours is
first-occurrence scoped-label replace --- \textbf{domain-preserving by
construction} --- which is what makes update's discharge free. The
novelty is being domain-preserving, not being typable at all.


\section{4 Metatheory: mechanized, argued,
refuted}\label{metatheory-mechanized-argued-refuted}

This section separates what is \emph{proved} (machine-checked in the
Lean development: 90 theorems, zero \texttt{sorry}, three explicit axiom
parameters --- \texttt{Unifies}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{Captures} at
\texttt{Typing.\allowbreak{}lean:221,229}, the unifier abstracted as a parameter of
the theory, and \texttt{unifies\_\allowbreak{}field\_\allowbreak{}projection} at
\texttt{Preserve.\allowbreak{}lean:213}; \texttt{lake\ build} clean), what is
\emph{measured} (fixtures, re-run in the gate), and what is
\emph{argued} (stated with its mechanism, not proved). The negative
result is \emph{stated, not proved}; it is the necessity direction, and
its mechanism is measured.

\subsection{4.1 The architecture: unification as a
parameter}\label{the-architecture-unification-as-a-parameter}

The typing judgment is mechanized constraint-based
(\texttt{Typing.\allowbreak{}lean}): the rules \emph{emit} unification constraints
against the abstract relation \texttt{Unifies\ R\ t₁\ t₂} and capture
equations through the abstract \texttt{Captures\ R\ t\_\allowbreak{}p\ t\_\allowbreak{}s\ Δᵢ} ---
no unification algorithm appears inside the rules, and no substitution
is threaded through them. Soundness of the calculus then requires the
unifier to be \emph{sound} (it must not accept inconsistent
constraints), not \emph{complete} --- which separates the row-specific
obligations from the (undecidable-complete) unifier problem. The store
discipline is visible in the rule shapes: \texttt{Has\allowbreak{}Type\allowbreak{}Branches}
threads one snapshot Δ; each branch body is checked under
\texttt{Δᵢ\ ++\ Δ} with its existentials added to R and its result check
run there; the recursion and the conclusion are back under the bare Δ.
The two-tier rule is verdict-indexed
(\texttt{Result\ Δ\ R\ t\_\allowbreak{}b\ t\_\allowbreak{}r\ v} with
\texttt{v\ ∈\ \{ok,\ escape\}}): Tier-T is a productive case (it
re-checks and may conclude ok); Tier-R is \emph{terminal} --- a needed
row equation forces escape. The asymmetry is in the type of the rule,
not merely in its premises. Theorems \texttt{tier\_\allowbreak{}R\_\allowbreak{}forces\_\allowbreak{}escape}
(\texttt{Typing\allowbreak{}Store.\allowbreak{}lean}) and \texttt{tier\_\allowbreak{}T\_\allowbreak{}ok}
(\texttt{Preserve.\allowbreak{}lean}) pin both directions.

\textbf{The assumption, named.} The theorems about the typing judgment
are conditional on the axiom parameters --- stated, not hidden: the
store discipline (\texttt{Typing\allowbreak{}Store.\allowbreak{}lean}) is conditional on
\texttt{Unifies}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{Captures} and on nothing else; the preservation
results (\texttt{Preserve.\allowbreak{}lean}) are conditional on the unifier being
\emph{sound} (it must not accept inconsistent constraints) and, for the
plain-selection case, on \texttt{unifies\_\allowbreak{}field\_\allowbreak{}projection} (the
discharged-selection and update cases need no unifier axiom). The
row-algebra theorems (H1, the domain rule, the update theorem, both
counterexamples) never mention the axioms. The correspondence between
the abstract relation and the implementation's unifier is
\emph{measured}, not proved: the gate's 154 checks, the approximation
inventory of Section 6.5, and the three-way agreement of Section 4.7
stand on the same boundary. Mechanizing the concrete row unifier against
these axioms is future work; it would discharge the assumption, not
change any theorem's statement.

\subsection{4.2 H1 --- rewrite/\allowbreak{}equation commutation, under
duplicates}\label{h1-rewriteequation-commutation-under-duplicates}

The genuinely novel formal content --- no prior system has the setting.
A branch's equation
\texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ ℓ\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}} is
\emph{consulted} by discharge, which reads the equation's head; the row
rewrite (scoped-label swap) is the operation that exposes a field of a
row. H1 says the two commute, and its hard case is \textbf{duplicate
labels}: a row may legally carry a duplicate ℓ \emph{before} the
equation's occurrence, in which case the first occurrence --- not the
equation's --- is what selection must expose.

The five mechanized theorems (\texttt{Row\allowbreak{}Gadt.\allowbreak{}lean}):

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{h1\_\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}commutes}} --- first-occurrence search
  commutes with scoped-label substitution: discharge-then-rewrite and
  rewrite-then-discharge agree.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{h1\_\allowbreak{}duplicate\_\allowbreak{}shadow}} --- a duplicate ℓ before the
  equation \emph{shadows} it: both routes expose the earlier field,
  never the equation's type. (This case was the open probe; the theorem
  is its confirmation.)
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{h1\_\allowbreak{}no\_\allowbreak{}shadow}} --- with no shadowing duplicate, the
  equation's head is what is selected (the positive counterpart).
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{h1\_\allowbreak{}head\_\allowbreak{}only\_\allowbreak{}vs\_\allowbreak{}full}} --- \textbf{the theorem
  that corrects the spec}: H1 read as ``for \emph{every} label m'' holds
  only in the \textbf{rigid-tail} regime; with a flex tail, the
  substitution-based search recurses into the tail while head-only
  discharge stops at the head. The weak form is what the implementation
  needs (and what we claim); the strong form is false as originally
  written in the companion spec.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{h1\_\allowbreak{}discharge\_\allowbreak{}head\_\allowbreak{}agrees}} --- the discharge's
  head-reading agrees with the full search on the equation's own label.
\end{itemize}

The corresponding probes exist and are pinned:
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}dup\_\allowbreak{}rebuild} (a full-duplicate rebuild is
\emph{accepted} --- the rebuild arm handles duplicate equation bodies)
and \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}dup\_\allowbreak{}fewer}, which pins the \emph{boundary} of this
story rather than H1 itself: it is a rebuild with \emph{fewer} duplicate
occurrences, and it is rejected --- the known false reject of the H2-b
domain rule, discussed under the escape coarseness below.

\subsection{4.3 H2-a --- store truncation}\label{h2-a-store-truncation}

Truncation is exact and nesting-safe \textbf{by construction} ---
restore assigns the snapshot prefix --- and the construction is
mechanized as three theorems (\texttt{h2a\_\allowbreak{}truncation},
\texttt{h2a\_\allowbreak{}no\_\allowbreak{}survival}, \texttt{h2a\_\allowbreak{}snapshot\_\allowbreak{}is\_\allowbreak{}suffix}, plus
\texttt{h2a\_\allowbreak{}inner\_\allowbreak{}snapshot\_\allowbreak{}suffix} for the nesting shape: an inner
branch's snapshot is a suffix of the outer store, so restore to a prefix
is well-defined at any depth).

\subsection{4.4 H2-b --- escape as a domain rule, and the two
counterexamples}\label{h2-b-escape-as-a-domain-rule-and-the-two-counterexamples}

H2-b is the obligation the adversarial hunt shaped (Section 6.2 states
the hunt; here is what it produced): \emph{no equation on a variable
free in the branch's result type may be needed to type that result} ---
including under an alias, which is where the real hole was. The
mechanized results:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{The domain rule.} \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}proper\_\allowbreak{}subdomain} (a refined
  tail is a proper sub-row of its head),
  \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}rejects\_\allowbreak{}tail} (the drop is rejected),
  \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}accepts\_\allowbreak{}rebuild} (the legitimate rebuild is
  accepted), \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}shrink}.
\item
  \textbf{Exactness, proved.} \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}exactness}: the rule
  is \textbf{exact for fresh labels and coarse for duplicates} --- the
  boundary is a theorem, not a hedge. The over-approximation is itself a
  theorem: \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}overapproximation} proves the \emph{old}
  syntactic predicate fires on a legitimate full-row rebuild ---
  i.e.~the old check's false reject was exactly the shape the domain
  rule fixes (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}shape\_\allowbreak{}rebuild} now compiles clean).
\item
  \textbf{Both counterexamples, mechanized.} The let-laundering hole is
  closed by \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}let\_\allowbreak{}severs\_\allowbreak{}occurs} +
  \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}rigid\_\allowbreak{}preserves\_\allowbreak{}occurs} and
  \textbf{\texttt{H2b\_\allowbreak{}no\_\allowbreak{}quantify\_\allowbreak{}refined\_\allowbreak{}tail}} (a refined tail is
  never quantified, so its occurrence survives generalization --- the
  generalization predicate \texttt{Generalizes\allowbreak{}Respects\allowbreak{}Refined} carries
  the exclusion, and \texttt{let\allowbreak{}R\_\allowbreak{}excludes\_\allowbreak{}refined\_\allowbreak{}tails} /
  \texttt{let\allowbreak{}R\_\allowbreak{}excludes\_\allowbreak{}refined\_\allowbreak{}body\_\allowbreak{}tails} consume R-LET's actual
  premises). The wildcard sibling leak is
  \textbf{\texttt{H2b\_\allowbreak{}wildcard\_\allowbreak{}leak\_\allowbreak{}shape}} +
  \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}direct\_\allowbreak{}collapses} (the \emph{symmetric} orientation the
  old check never tested) + \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}wildcard\_\allowbreak{}collapses}.
  \texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}alias\_\allowbreak{}identifies} covers the
  through-an-intermediate-variable aliasing.
\item
  \textbf{The residue is coarseness, not unsoundness.} A rebuild with
  \emph{fewer} duplicate occurrences than the equation body is a false
  reject (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}dup\_\allowbreak{}fewer} errs
  \texttt{cannot\ unify\ a\ with\ \{x:Int\textbar{}\ a\}} --- the pinned
  do-not-weaken fixture). An adversarial battery over duplicate shapes
  (bare tail return, let-laundered tail, wildcard sibling, wrong label,
  wrong first-occurrence type, wrong field type; re-homed in
  \texttt{examples/\allowbreak{}research/\allowbreak{}dup-\allowbreak{}hunt/\allowbreak{}}) found \textbf{no unsound
  accept}. The asymmetry is the useful part: H2 errs safe, and the
  battery bounds what it is missing.
\item
  \textbf{Result-scoping, measured.} The tail-aliasing check is
  \emph{result-scoped}, and so is the obligation: a branch may perform
  the same flex-tail-aliases-rigid-head identification in its body ---
  \texttt{select}'s \texttt{There} branch does, recursing on the tail
  --- provided the result type does not mention the row
  (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}select} stays clean). H2-b as stated is exactly
  result-scoped; strengthening it to ``no aliasing anywhere in the
  body'' is refuted by that fixture.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{4.5 The update theorem and its
dual}\label{the-update-theorem-and-its-dual}

The positive row result is mechanized (\texttt{Update.\allowbreak{}lean}, reusing
\texttt{Row\allowbreak{}Gadt}'s row algebra): \texttt{update\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}preserving}
(update preserves the row's domain: restrict-then-re-prepend of the
existing first occurrence), \texttt{update\_\allowbreak{}reflexive\_\allowbreak{}domain},
\textbf{\texttt{update\_\allowbreak{}accepted\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}rho}} (under
\texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ ℓ\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}}, update
is well-typed at the abstract ρ with no discharge and no binding), and
--- the dual --- \texttt{insertion\_\allowbreak{}fresh\_\allowbreak{}extends},
\texttt{insertion\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}exactness},
\textbf{\texttt{insertion\_\allowbreak{}rejected\_\allowbreak{}under\_\allowbreak{}refinement}} (a fresh-label
insertion strictly extends the domain, which is why it may never consult
the store), \texttt{insertion\_\allowbreak{}shadow\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}unchanged}. The
restriction side of R-UPD-INS is itself mechanized in the typing arc:
\texttt{refined\allowbreak{}Tail\allowbreak{}Var\_\allowbreak{}iff\_\allowbreak{}insertion\allowbreak{}Rejected} ties the rejection
predicate to the store's refined-tail lookup, and
\texttt{insertion\allowbreak{}Rejected\_\allowbreak{}mono\_\allowbreak{}left/\allowbreak{}right} prove the monotonicity the
rule relies on.

\subsection{4.6 Preservation of the record
operations}\label{preservation-of-the-record-operations}

The deadline-grade slice of T2 is mechanized in \texttt{Preserve.\allowbreak{}lean}:
a minimal small-step relation with exactly the two record reductions
(selection by first-occurrence lookup; update by cons-prepend-shadow ---
the \emph{measured} dynamic semantics: records lower to association
lists and \texttt{assoc} is first-match-from-head, the same
first-occurrence discipline the rewrite uses), plus
\texttt{record\_\allowbreak{}first\_\allowbreak{}occ} /\allowbreak{} \texttt{record\_\allowbreak{}domain} (the
static/\allowbreak{}dynamic first-occurrence correspondence).
\texttt{sel\_\allowbreak{}preserves}, \textbf{\texttt{sel\allowbreak{}Disch\_\allowbreak{}preserves}} (the
\emph{discharged} selection --- the refinement-licensed one ---
preserves types), \texttt{upd\_\allowbreak{}preserves}, and the step-level forms
(\texttt{sel\_\allowbreak{}step\_\allowbreak{}preserves}, \texttt{sel\allowbreak{}Disch\_\allowbreak{}step\_\allowbreak{}preserves},
\texttt{upd\_\allowbreak{}step\_\allowbreak{}preserves}), with \texttt{first\allowbreak{}Type\_\allowbreak{}subst\_\allowbreak{}rowvar}
as the full-grammar restatement of \texttt{h1\_\allowbreak{}no\_\allowbreak{}shadow}. The
discharged selection and the update cases need \textbf{no} unifier
axiom; the plain selection case is conditional on
\texttt{unifies\_\allowbreak{}field\_\allowbreak{}projection} (that unifying two record types
relates the first-occurrence types of a common label) --- stated as an
axiom parameter alongside \texttt{Unifies}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{Captures}.

\subsection{4.7 What is argued, and the negative
result}\label{what-is-argued-and-the-negative-result}

\textbf{No general soundness theorem exists for λρG.} T1 (progress) and
T2 (preservation) are argued, not proved: T1 introduces no new redex
shape and its genuinely new obligation --- every selection licensed by
R-SEL-DISCH finds its label at runtime --- is \emph{carried by} T2's
SELECT clause, which is what \texttt{sel\allowbreak{}Disch\_\allowbreak{}preserves} mechanizes;
T2's two row clauses are exactly what H1 and the update theorem carry.
What the mechanization \emph{does} prove are typing-judgment theorems
--- the row algebra, the store discipline
(\texttt{tier\_\allowbreak{}R\_\allowbreak{}forces\_\allowbreak{}escape} and companions), the escape rule, and
record-operation preservation --- conditional on the unifier abstracted
as a parameter (Section 4.1); it does not attempt the whole calculus. We
say this once, plainly, and do not let later sections upgrade ``argued''
to ``proved''.

\textbf{The negative result (stated, not proved).} Let λρG⁻ be the
variant in which branch mode is replaced by global mode: a branch's
would-be capture is solved into θ. Then λρG⁻ types programs whose
exported scheme lies about row domains. For \texttt{select} (Figure 1):
the \texttt{Here} branch's equation is
\texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ l\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ₁\ \}}, the \texttt{There}
branch's is \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ k\ :\ s\ \textbar{}\ ρ₂\ \}}; sequential
clause checking solves the first into θ, and the second either fails
spuriously (the \emph{policy} shape --- today's rigid guard's rejection)
or, with the guard removed, silently overwrites --- and the exported
scheme \texttt{∀ρ\ l\ t.\allowbreak{}\ Has\ l\ t\ ρ\ →\ \{ρ\}\ →\ t} keeps promising
nothing about \texttt{l}, while the body's \texttt{r.\allowbreak{}l} was justified by
it. The mechanism is measured, twice, in the implementation's own
history: the pre-discharge classic case bound \texttt{a\ :=\ Int}
globally at the definition while call sites kept
\texttt{∀\ a.\allowbreak{}\ Expr\ a\ →\ a} --- silent wrong code
(\texttt{eval\allowbreak{}Int\ (Bool\allowbreak{}Lit\ True)} typechecked at \texttt{Bool} and
would crash); and the five unsound accepts of Section 6.2 are the same
class of defect --- a branch equation that should not survive its branch
either escaping it or dying without its occurs check. So: the discipline
is \textbf{necessary} (this theorem-shaped statement, with its mechanism
measured) and \textbf{sufficient for every program in the corpus and the
designed fixtures} (125 gate checks on the typing surface --- the gate
total is 154, the other 29 being frontend lambda-lift fixtures, which do
not exercise the escape rule; the three-pass hunt closed all five
unsound accepts, and found none after the final class-level repair) ---
sufficiency over \emph{all} programs is \textbf{not} proved, and is not
claimed.

\textbf{Three-way agreement.} The escape boundary is corroborated in
three independent places: the Lean theorem
(\texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}exactness}: exact for fresh labels, coarse for
duplicates), the implementation's own exactness note (the rebuild arm
accepts exact field-list matches; the fewer-duplicate rebuild is a false
reject), and the duplicate-shape adversarial battery (no unsound accept,
the one clean accept being the exact full rebuild \texttt{e3\_\allowbreak{}swap}).
The proof, the implementation, and the probes agree on both the rule and
its boundary --- that agreement is the paper's metatheory story.


\section{5 The principality boundary}\label{the-principality-boundary}

The discipline has a cost, and the cost is \emph{located} --- and the
location is counterintuitive.

\subsection{5.1 The boundary, stated}\label{the-boundary-stated}

Principal types are retained in the fragment we call \textbf{P}:
programs where every refinement's target is either (a) a branch-scoped
existential --- the constructor's own variable, rigid \emph{within} its
branch by R-EXISTS --- or (b) discharged inside the branch. Plain row
code (no GADT) is the degenerate case: \texttt{f\ rec\ =\ rec.\allowbreak{}x} infers
\texttt{∀\ r\ a.\ \{\ r\ \textbar{}\ x\ :\ a\ \}\ →\ a}, as Leijen's
principality result says it must.

Principality is lost in the fragment we call \textbf{Q}: exactly when
two sibling branches refine the same \emph{signature} row variable and
the result type mentions it. In Q there is no principal monotype. The
two clauses of \texttt{select} infer monotypes that cannot be unified:

{\footnotesize\begin{verbatim}
select Here  r = r.l              --  Has l t { l : t | ρ₁ } → { l : t | ρ₁ } → t
select There h r = select h r     --  Has l t { k : s | ρ₂ } → { k : s | ρ₂ } → t
\end{verbatim}}

for distinct \texttt{l\ ≠\ k} there is no single row substitution that
solves both equations, so the inferred monotype does not exist --- only
the \emph{scheme-with-store} reading, which is to say: the signature
\texttt{∀\ ρ\ l\ t.\allowbreak{}\ Has\ l\ t\ ρ\ →\ \{ρ\}\ →\ t} is \textbf{checkable,
not inferable}. This is precisely the locally-abstract-types dependency:
rigidity is what makes the signature checkable under conflicting branch
equations, and the signature is not optional in Q.

\subsection{5.2 The measurement, and the
inversion}\label{the-measurement-and-the-inversion}

The L3 table (Figure 5): three presentations of the \emph{same access}
--- read a field justified by a witness --- with the signature
\emph{omitted}, all three gate-registered and re-measured:
