\textbf{Figure 5.} The L3 principality measurement --- three
presentations of the same access, the signature omitted. Source: gate
fixtures \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}l3i}, \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}l3ii},
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}l3iii} (measured column, re-measured by the artifact's
verification script; registered rows in
\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}fixtures/\allowbreak{}MATRIX.\allowbreak{}md}); the P/\allowbreak{}Q classification is §5.1
above (\texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}research/\allowbreak{}row-\allowbreak{}gadt.\allowbreak{}md} §5).

The middle row is the boundary of Section 5.1, measured. But the
informative comparison is (i) vs (ii): the \emph{encoded} presentation
sits on the \textbf{P side} while its \emph{native translation} sits on
the \textbf{Q side}. The witness encoding does not merely model rows ---
\textbf{it moves the principality boundary}. The reason is structural:
in the encoded presentation the recovered element type is a
\emph{constructor existential}, rigid within its branch by R-EXISTS, so
inference proceeds without a signature; in the native form the recovered
row refines a \emph{signature} variable, which must be rigid for the
sibling branches to agree --- and a signature-directed rigidity cannot
be recovered by inference.

We record the history because it is itself evidence: our pre-measurement
guess had the two sides \textbf{swapped} (we expected witnesses to lack
principal types). The measurement is the result, and the guess is not
published as one.

\textbf{The price of the encoding.} The P side is bought at the cost of
expressible operations: the encoded presentation has no update (an HList
cons-cell rebuild is not a record update), no domain restriction, and
the absent-field negative --- the \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}absentfield}
rejection that Section 2.4 uses to \emph{bound} what refinement licenses
--- cannot even be \emph{stated} in it. The boundary is a trade, not a
ranking: the encoding buys inference and loses the operation inventory.

\subsection{5.3 What position-directed rigidity does and does not
move}\label{what-position-directed-rigidity-does-and-does-not-move}

The rigidity work (Section 6.3) was measured against this boundary and
does \textbf{not} move it: \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}l3ii}'s \texttt{select} is
\emph{unsignatured}, and a signature-directed rule cannot reach an
unsignatured definition, so the Q-side rejection stands. What the change
did flip is the closely-related bare \emph{HList} form ---
\texttt{hget\ :\ Has\ l\ t\ rho\ →\ HList\ rho\ →\ t} with no binder,
which conflicted at its recursive \texttt{There} call before and now
checks clean (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}hget\_\allowbreak{}bare}). The honest reading: the P/\allowbreak{}Q
line sits where it was --- a signature is required exactly where two
sibling branches need different equations on a signature variable whose
result mentions it --- and the narrow delta (bare \texttt{hget}
checkable, rigidity systematic rather than per-branch) is the
\emph{structural} value of the change: it closes the
should-be-rigid-treated-as-solvable bug class at its root instead of per
case.


\section{6 Implementation and measured
correspondence}\label{implementation-and-measured-correspondence}

The discipline is not a paper design with a sketch: it runs inside a
real checker. The substrate is an Elm-family compiler with
Hindley--Milner inference over Leijen scoped-label rows (the
pre-existing \texttt{elm-\allowbreak{}compiler/\allowbreak{}src/\allowbreak{}Type/\allowbreak{}*} tree: unification with a
row-rewrite, let generalization, an eight-library corpus and a self-host
track). The change is contained to the pattern path and the unifier
state; lowering and codegen are untouched (types are erased) --- nor was
the interpreter back end, while it existed. Everything below is
\emph{measured}, and every number is reproducible from the artifact by
one command (the artifact's verification script, which rebuilds the
compiler, runs the gate, checks the corpus byte-identity, runs the unit
suite, builds the Lean project, and re-derives the interpreter recount;
its output is the source of every number printed here --- run on the
current tree of the artifact repository. The frozen artifact tag
(annotated; it dereferences to the commit it was made on) predates the
final commits, which touch the documentation, the gate and
reproducibility scripts, and the generated fixture registry this paper
cites, and the codegen backend, whose ZINC interpreter was retired; the
counts printed here are the current tree's, not the tag's, and the
Appendix A correction records both. The implementation was split out of
the host project that previously contained it: the import brought the
tree across from the host's then-HEAD, eight commits ahead of the freeze
tag marking the pre-adversarial-pass baseline, with two further
host-side commits following; the language was later removed from the
host and the UI parked. The arrow-spelling GADT parser fix, the
equation-lifecycle repair, and the lambda-lifting pass all post-date the
freeze tag).

\textbf{A substrate fact, recorded as an artifact datum.} The
substrate's local \texttt{let} is \emph{sequential-only}: a local
function cannot see its own name, so a self-recursive local helper fails
\texttt{type\ error\ …\ unknown\ name:\ f} (raised by the checker,
before lowering). The compiler's own \texttt{Type/\allowbreak{}Exhaustive.\allowbreak{}elm} (its
\texttt{resolve\allowbreak{}Scrutinee}) hit this while the compiler's sources were
being made self-hosting; a frontend lambda-lifting pass now hoists
recursive local groups to the top level
(\texttt{elm-\allowbreak{}compiler/\allowbreak{}src/\allowbreak{}Frontend/\allowbreak{}Lift.\allowbreak{}elm}), with the VM substrate
untouched --- no new instruction and no collector change, which is why a
frontend pass was chosen over a VM-level \texttt{letrec}. It is recorded
as a measured datum about what the substrate is and what the artifact
needed, not as a contribution.

\textbf{The non-regression invariant.} The corpus --- the compiler's own
eight core libraries, the prelude, and the runtime, as compiled
artifacts --- must be \textbf{byte-identical} before and after the
change: the 149 compiled artifacts match a committed sha256 manifest
entry-for-entry with zero moved (re-measured, exit 0). This invariant is
what makes the discipline's addition safe to \emph{adopt}, and the
design pays for it deliberately: the historical inference path remains
primary; the new machinery (branch-local capture, discharge, the
declaration-directed retry) engages only where the historical path fails
--- so every pre-existing diagnostic is unchanged by construction. The
regression gate passes 154/\allowbreak{}154 (the designed-fixture matrix with
expected outcomes is Table 1 in Appendix A, the complete generated
registry is \texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}fixtures/\allowbreak{}MATRIX.\allowbreak{}md}, and the gate is
\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}fixtures/\allowbreak{}run-\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}gate.\allowbreak{}sh}), and the unit suite passes
95/\allowbreak{}95.

\subsection{6.1 What the build surfaced:
kinds}\label{what-the-build-surfaced-kinds}

The first four implementation blockers the build hit were all
\emph{pre-existing substrate defects}, reproducible without any GADT,
and \textbf{three of the four were kinding defects}:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  ADT generics were forced to \texttt{KType}, so a generic used at a
  row-tail position mis-kinded (\texttt{Has\ l\ t\ ρ} with ρ used as a
  record tail). Fixed by kinding generics from their use position.
\item
  Kind inference by first \emph{use} position then broke the other
  source order --- the same declaration mis-kinded depending on whether
  the tail use preceded the index use. Fixed with a row-tail
  \textbf{prescan} that binds record-tail names to \texttt{KRow} before
  conversion (\texttt{collect\allowbreak{}File\allowbreak{}Type\allowbreak{}Kinds}).
\item
  The unifier had no path for a bare \texttt{KRow} variable against a
  record type --- exactly the shape a GADT constructor's result index
  produces. Routed to the row binder in \textbf{branch mode only} (the
  global path keeps its historical behaviour; the
  bare-\texttt{KRow}-vs-record gap is still measureable outside branch
  mode --- see the \texttt{read} reducer in Section 1.4).
\item
  A flex-alias wrapper bug: the flex row variable was bound to the
  record \emph{wrapper} rather than to the variable, so a rigid variable
  meeting its own alias was rejected. Fixed in the identity case.
\end{enumerate}

The finding generalizes: \textbf{a calculus without explicit row kinds
cannot predict where a real implementation breaks.} The declarative spec
states the kind of every declaration; the implementation
\emph{elaborates} it from the surface (because the surface has no kind
annotations), and the elaboration rules were built precisely because
first-use inference mis-kinded order-dependent programs. This is why λρG
carries kinds in its syntax (Section 2) rather than as a periphery.

\subsection{6.2 The escape check's evolution --- the section's
centrepiece}\label{the-escape-checks-evolution-the-sections-centrepiece}

The branch-result escape rule (Section 3.1's Tier-R) went through three
measured stages, and the stages are the paper's honesty about its own
metatheory.

\textbf{(1) The first check was syntactic} --- a tail-occurrence test in
one orientation: reject when the refined row's \emph{tail} variable
appears in the body's type while the \emph{head} appears in the expected
result. It was sound on the shapes its author considered.

\textbf{(2) The first of three adversarial passes found two programs the
check accepted that are unsound} (both are now gate-registered compile
errors, \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}escape\_\allowbreak{}launder} and
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}escape\_\allowbreak{}wildcard}; both programs in full, verbatim, are
Figure 6):

\begin{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Let-laundering.} The \texttt{Here} branch refines
  \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ l\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}}, the
  scrutinee is an \texttt{HList\ ρ}, and the branch returns its tail ---
  laundered through a \texttt{let} (Figure 6a).

  \texttt{let}-generalization \emph{quantified the refined tail} ρ', so
  the use of \texttt{ys} instantiates a fresh variable with no link to
  the tail; the occurrence test sees nothing; the fresh variable then
  legally aliases the rigid head. The returned list is missing field
  \texttt{l} --- an unsound accept (the pre-fix checker compiled it
  clean).
\item
  \textbf{Wildcard sibling leak.} The refining branch returns the tail
  while a wildcard branch returns the full row (Figure 6b).

  The shared case-result variable lets the wildcard's full-row result
  unify \emph{tail := head} --- a legal flex alias --- zonking the tail
  away before the clause-level check runs. The check had been written in
  one orientation only; the sibling branch smuggled the identification
  past it.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{(a) Let-laundering} --- verbatim from
\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}fixtures/\allowbreak{}rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}escape\_\allowbreak{}launder.\allowbreak{}elm} (lines 11--31):

{\normalsize\begin{verbatim}
type Has l t rho
    = Here : Has l t { l : t | rho }
    | There : Has l t rho -> Has l t { k : s | rho }


type HList rho
    = HNil : HList {}
    | HCons : t -> HList rho -> HList { l : t | rho }


escapeBad : type l t rho. Has l t rho -> HList rho -> HList rho
escapeBad h xs =
    case ( h, xs ) of
        ( Here, HCons _ rest ) ->
            let
                ys = rest
            in
            ys

        ( There h2, HCons _ rest ) ->
            escapeBad h2 rest
\end{verbatim}}

\textbf{(b) Wildcard sibling leak} --- verbatim from
\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}fixtures/\allowbreak{}rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}escape\_\allowbreak{}wildcard.\allowbreak{}elm} (lines
11--27):

{\normalsize\begin{verbatim}
type Has l t rho
    = Here : Has l t { l : t | rho }


type HList rho
    = HNil : HList {}
    | HCons : t -> HList rho -> HList { l : t | rho }


escapeBad : type l t rho. Has l t rho -> HList rho -> HList rho
escapeBad h xs =
    case ( h, xs ) of
        ( Here, HCons _ rest ) ->
            rest

        _ ->
            xs
\end{verbatim}}

\textbf{Figure 6.} The two stage-(2) counterexamples. Pre-fix, both
compiled clean (unsound accepts); post-fix, both are gate-registered
compile errors, \texttt{err\ escaping\ row\ equation\ …} (Table 1).

\textbf{(3) The rule is now domain-based}, and the domain rule is what
the mechanization proves sound. At a branch result whose unification
fails on a refined rigid row head, the check decides on the
\emph{domain}, not on syntactic occurrence: \textbf{drop} (the
unification newly identified the tail with the head ---
\texttt{drop\allowbreak{}Introduced} compares the tail-reach before and after this
step) → reject; \textbf{rebuild} (the presented row unifies with the
equation's body, and the head does not occur in it) → \emph{accept};
anything else → reject (code seats: \texttt{tail\allowbreak{}Reaches\allowbreak{}Head},
\texttt{drop\allowbreak{}Introduced}, \texttt{rebuild\allowbreak{}Matches} in
\texttt{Type/\allowbreak{}Infer.\allowbreak{}elm}). The rebuild arm is what makes the rule
\emph{complete enough to be usable}: returning the scrutinee rebuilt ---
\texttt{HCons\ x\ rest} at
\texttt{HList\ \{\ l\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}}, whose
domain equals the head's under the equation --- is a \emph{legitimate}
return that the syntactic check false-rejected
(\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}shape\_\allowbreak{}rebuild}, clean). Both fixes and the rebuild
acceptance are pinned; six further must-error escape shapes were
re-verified after the change.

\textbf{The two passes after the escape check.} The escape rule was only
the \emph{first} adversarial target. A second pass attacked the checks
\emph{as they ship} --- the previous pass had only ever attacked the
rule it replaced --- and found two more unsound accepts. \textbf{CE-1},
a \texttt{drop\allowbreak{}Introduced} scoping bypass: the body pre-aliased the
refined tail to its head \emph{before} the result unify, outside the
window the check observed (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}ce1\_\allowbreak{}prealias}).
\textbf{CE-2}, a bare-variable scrutinee over-generalisation that also
hit \emph{plain ADTs}: matching a bare scrutinee lifted and then dropped
its index equation, over-generalising to \texttt{∀a.\allowbreak{}\ a\ →\ r} and
over-refuting the sibling, so \texttt{f\ B} compiled clean and crashed
at runtime (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}ce2\_\allowbreak{}barevar}; the same defect in a
non-GADT form, \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}ce2\_\allowbreak{}plain}). A third pass attacked the
\emph{coercion surface} --- the Tier-T result-unify path the whole
two-tier rule rests on, which had been assumed correct rather than
tested --- and found the most serious accept so far: a
\textbf{wrong-typed value}, not a crash.
\texttt{Mk\allowbreak{}Box\ :\ a\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ Box\ (List\ a)} with
\texttt{get\ b\ =\ case\ b\ of\ Mk\allowbreak{}Box\ v\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ v} accepted
\texttt{get\ (Mk\allowbreak{}Box\ 3)} at \texttt{List\ Int} while its value is the
\texttt{Int} \texttt{3}, because the flex→rigid alias bound the equation
\texttt{a\ \textasciitilde{}\ List\ a} without ever occurs-checking it
(\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}ce3\_\allowbreak{}fieldalias}). A per-shape guard
(\texttt{refined\allowbreak{}Target\allowbreak{}Aliased\allowbreak{}By}) closed that one shape, but a review
found \textbf{three bypasses} of it --- the alias forming inside a
tuple, before the result unify, and through a \texttt{let} --- each
compiling clean and printing a wrong-typed value. The real cause was the
\textbf{equation lifecycle}: a pending \texttt{KType} equation must be
occurs-checked before it is discarded or a result accepted; the repair
(\texttt{pending\allowbreak{}Type\allowbreak{}Occurs}) does exactly that, and all three bypasses
now error \texttt{infinite\ type} (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}ce3a\_\allowbreak{}tuple},
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}ce3b\_\allowbreak{}prealias}, \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}ce3c\_\allowbreak{}let}). In
total: three passes, five unsound accepts, one class-level repair.

The stage-(2) lesson is methodological and worth stating: the hunt was
run \emph{before} the mechanization, and H2 as first conceived was the
wrong shape of lemma --- a statement constraining only the branch-result
unification cannot see the let-form leak. Had the theorem been proved
first, it would have enshrined a property the implementation did not
enforce. Section 4 gives the mechanized form of both counterexamples
(\texttt{H2b\_\allowbreak{}no\_\allowbreak{}quantify\_\allowbreak{}refined\_\allowbreak{}tail},
\texttt{H2b\_\allowbreak{}wildcard\_\allowbreak{}leak\_\allowbreak{}shape}) as part of the metatheory, not as
an appendix.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{6.3 The \texttt{type\ a.} surface and the
too-general
police}{6.3 The type a. surface and the too-general police}}\label{the-type-a.-surface-and-the-too-general-police}

The surface prefix \texttt{type\ x̂₁\ …\ x̂ₙ.} names the signature
quantifiers that are \textbf{rigid while the body is checked}; unnamed
quantifiers stay flexible, and soundness is restored \emph{after} the
body by the \textbf{too-general police} --- a re-check that skolemizes
the declared scheme and unifies it against the generalized body type,
rejecting ``annotation is too general''. The measured asymmetry is
exactly the design's prediction: the binder'd \texttt{select} checks;
the same body without the binder is rejected --- either by the
conflicting-equations failure
(\texttt{cannot\ unify\ \{k:a\textbar{}\ b\}\ with\ \{\textbar{}\ a\}},
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}l3ii}) or, for classic GADTs, by the police
(``annotation is too general''). Rigidity is the mechanism; the prefix
is its surface.

\textbf{Position-directed rigidity.} A signature variable at a
\emph{direct GADT-index position} (\texttt{Has\ l\ t\ ρ},
\texttt{Expr\ a}) is rigid whether or not the surface binds it: the
checker collects the file's own annotated-result constructors and their
index variables (\texttt{collect\allowbreak{}Gadt\allowbreak{}Names} /\allowbreak{} \texttt{gadt\allowbreak{}Index\allowbreak{}Vars})
into the scheme's bound set, so
\texttt{hget\ :\ Has\ l\ t\ rho\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ HList\ rho\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ t}
--- with \textbf{no} binder --- now checks identically to its binder'd
form (this specific program flipped from rejected to clean and is
pinned: \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}hget\_\allowbreak{}bare}). The measurement was honest about
its own narrowness: bare \texttt{select}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{eval} \emph{already}
compiled clean (the per-branch index lift covered them), and the
principality boundary of Section 5 does \textbf{not} move
(\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}l3ii} is an \emph{unsignatured} definition, which a
signature-directed rule cannot reach). The value of the change is
structural --- it closes the recurring ``should-be-rigid variable
treated as solvable'' bug class at its root, and it is what makes the
refutation guard of Section 1.4 sound at a \emph{bare} index
(\texttt{refutbare}).

\subsection{6.4 The compiler's own effect
interpreter}\label{the-compilers-own-effect-interpreter}

\textbf{An artifact datum, recorded as such.} The \texttt{Task} type now
declares only the effects its host can perform --- the ten UI effect
constructors and the \texttt{Key}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{Mouse} types left the language
and park in the host project pending a UI redesign --- and an effect the
host does not implement fails loudly and terminates, pinned by a
hand-crafted-bundle gate check (\texttt{unhandledtask}). It is recorded
as a datum about what the artifact now is, not as a contribution.

The acid test is not a fixture but the compiler's own
\texttt{Runtime.\allowbreak{}run\allowbreak{}Task} --- the free-monad interpreter for its
20-constructor effect type, historically a \emph{trusted body} (a
function the checker skips, with a lie for a type). The trusted comment
stated its own retirement precondition: kept trusted ``until the
per-ctor result table can drive a checked interpreter''. The machinery
of this paper is that table's typability condition, so we tested it.

\textbf{The precondition was met, mechanically.} The 20 per-ctor result
annotations (\texttt{Task\allowbreak{}Exec\ a\ :\ Task\ x\ (Int,\ String,\ String)}
--- real source syntax in \texttt{Runtime.\allowbreak{}elm}, migrated from a
hardcoded table) were proven behaviour-preserving by \emph{two
independent oracles}: the inferred constructor schemes were
byte-identical before/\allowbreak{}after the migration (20/\allowbreak{}20), and the full corpus
compiled byte-identically.

\textbf{And it was not sufficient --- a fail-fast artifact.} Un-trusting
\texttt{run\allowbreak{}Task} (removing it from the trusted list) reports exactly
\emph{one} error, at \texttt{Task\allowbreak{}Exec}, and stops: a checker that halts
at the first error cannot see the branches behind it. Masking each
failing branch in source order to reveal the next (a reproducible
bisection script, the recount script, which edits only a scratch copy
and asserts every step's expected error) gives \textbf{four} failing
branches --- so the honest count is \textbf{16 of 20 branches check
honestly}, and the earlier ``29 of 30'' figure was this fail-fast
artifact (in the 30-constructor era, before the UI effects left the
\texttt{Task} type). The four, named:

{

  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}

\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright

\end{minipage} \\

\texttt{Task\allowbreak{}Exec} & payload \texttt{a} vs
\texttt{exec\allowbreak{}Plan\allowbreak{}Prim\ :\ List\ a\ →\ List\ b} needs
\texttt{a\ ≐\ List\ a} & \textbf{defect}: a dynamic cast \\
\texttt{Task\allowbreak{}Now} & \texttt{Ok\ 0} number literal hits flex-marker

One of the four is \emph{design, not defect}: \texttt{Task\allowbreak{}Quit} is the
one constructor the annotation table deliberately left generalized, and
the bisection's own terminal signal proves the list is closed --- after
masking the fourth failure the trivial fixture compiles \textbf{clean},
the no-fifth-branch evidence. The composition of the holdouts moved, and
the paper says so rather than reading the new figure as a code change:
\texttt{Task\allowbreak{}Gui\allowbreak{}Poll}, the second deliberate holdout of the
30-constructor era, left the \texttt{Task} type with the UI effects ---
and with it went the old terminal signal (a \texttt{Tea.\allowbreak{}Gui\allowbreak{}Ev} call-site
cascade at a \texttt{Task.\allowbreak{}perform} use), which was the earlier evidence
that annotating the generalized constructors would break their callers'
deliberate polymorphism. The count has one stated condition: it is taken
under a \texttt{type\ x\ a.} binder (the committed signature has none;
without the binder the flexible index is bound by the first
concrete-result branch and the later branches cascade --- the discharge
being measured requires the rigid index). The condition is printed by
the recount script, not hidden.

\textbf{The residue is a representation problem, not a refinement one.}
\texttt{Task\allowbreak{}Exec}'s payload is typed \texttt{a} --- the constructor's
existential, absent from its result --- while the runtime value
\emph{is} a tagged list; no refinement of an abstract variable expresses
\texttt{a\ ≐\ List\ a}. The honest fix is a surface change (type the
payload \texttt{List\ a}), not more type theory. The rest of the trusted
list decomposes the same way: the remaining trusted bodies are lies of
\emph{representation} (the VM value is uniformly typed; \texttt{compare}
introspects it), not of refinement. An experiment with an honest
\texttt{Value} datatype (\texttt{probe\allowbreak{}A}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{probe\allowbreak{}A2} in
\texttt{examples/\allowbreak{}research/\allowbreak{}}) confirms it: with honest constructors, the
\texttt{compare}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{decode*} bodies type-check clean, and a
deliberately wrong body is still rejected --- the checker's discipline
is intact; what is missing is an honest datatype, not an equation.

\subsection{6.5 The measured correspondence to the
calculus}\label{the-measured-correspondence-to-the-calculus}

Where the implementation approximates the declarative rules (the
calculus's own {[}U{]}/\allowbreak{}{[}S{]} inventory, compressed):

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{The two-pass retry --- {[}S{]}, soundness-neutral.} The
  implementation checks a signatured declaration's clauses bottom-up,
  and only on failure with a directly-case body retries
  declaration-directed (each branch against the declared result, each
  with its own discharges). The \emph{declarative calculus has only the
  declaration-directed rule}. The retry accepts a subset: the canonical
  evaluator wrapped in a \texttt{let} is spuriously rejected
  (\texttt{g\allowbreak{}Neg\_\allowbreak{}letcase}, re-homed and re-measured:
  \texttt{cannot\ unify\ Bool\ with\ Int}). No completeness claim is
  made for the retry path.
\item
  \textbf{Per-file kinding --- {[}U, weakly{]}.} ADT generic kinds are
  collected per file, so a cross-file bare row parameter could kind as a
  type variable (turning a row equation into a type equation Tier-T
  would discharge). Unexercised by the corpus and fixtures; stated as an
  approximation.
\item
  \textbf{The duplicate-label coarseness --- {[}S{]}, proved and
  pinned.} The rebuild arm requires an \emph{exact} unification with the
  equation body, so a body rebuilding with fewer duplicate occurrences
  is a false reject (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}dup\_\allowbreak{}fewer}, with a do-not-weaken
  comment); the domain rule's exactness boundary is a theorem
  (\texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}exactness}, Section 4).
\item
  \textbf{Trusted bodies and surface restrictions --- {[}S{]}.} The
  fixed trusted list is modelled as an escape, not a rule; the surface
  has no type-level strings; record literals are closed (an open row can
  only be \emph{named}, never constructed);
  \texttt{\{\ \textbar{}\ ρ\ \}} bare-open does not parse; the update
  base must be a local variable.
\item
  \textbf{Exhaustiveness and refutation --- {[}S{]}, an addition.} The
  calculus's case rule now carries a compile-time exhaustiveness and
  refutation check (\texttt{Type/\allowbreak{}Exhaustive.\allowbreak{}elm}): a missing possible
  arm is an error; an impossible arm under the branch equations is
  refuted and not required. The check's own boundary is measured and
  pinned: refutation fires only at a concrete or binder-rigid index
  (\texttt{refutbare}); a \emph{pre-existing} false positive for
  unsignatured nested patterns (\texttt{Just\ (a,\ b)} vs
  \texttt{Just\ \_}) remains, and is not a soundness issue.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{6.6 Runnability: the gate now executes, not just
compiles}\label{runnability-the-gate-now-executes-not-just-compiles}

The \texttt{compile\_\allowbreak{}clean} gate check asserts only that compilation
\emph{succeeds} --- it never runs the result --- so a lowering or arity
bug in the GADT path was invisible for the whole project, until one was
found: a GADT constructor in the arrow spelling
\texttt{C\ :\ A\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ B\ -\allowbreak{}\textgreater{}\ T} parsed with
\texttt{arguments\ =\ {[}{]}}, so the lowerer emitted an arity-0
constructor and \emph{applying} it crashed
(\texttt{apply\ non-\allowbreak{}callable}), while the type checker was happy because
the result annotation is a function type. Seven GADT fixtures were
converted from \texttt{compile\_\allowbreak{}clean} to real \texttt{run} checks with
pinned outputs --- \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}eval}
\texttt{{[}cons\ 1\ .\allowbreak{}\ true{]}}, \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}het} \texttt{"hi3"},
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}l3i} \texttt{"3"}, \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}l3iii} \texttt{1},
\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}fsm} \texttt{"open:42"}, \texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}fsm\_\allowbreak{}nested}
\texttt{"open:42"}, \texttt{refutpos} \texttt{5} --- so the gate now
\emph{executes} the GADT path, and this arity class is a regression
fixture rather than an invisible gap.

\subsection{6.7 Provenance: AI assistance in building this
artifact}\label{provenance-ai-assistance-in-building-this-artifact}

The ACM Policy on Authorship requires AI use that \emph{conducts the
research} --- designing the methodology, implementing, testing,
validating, and archiving the artifacts the conclusions rest on --- to
be described in detail in the methods section of the work; AI assistance
with the \emph{writing} no longer requires disclosure. This subsection
is that description (§6 is this paper's methods section). It is a
statement about process, not about the discipline.

\textbf{Where the assistance was.} AI coding agents, working from the
author's briefs and reviewed by the author, produced the project's own
code, by area: the compiler implementation --- the Elm-family compiler
and its Hindley--Milner checker over scoped-label rows
(\texttt{elm-\allowbreak{}compiler/\allowbreak{}src/\allowbreak{}}, including the eight core libraries), the
frontend lambda-lifting pass
(\texttt{elm-\allowbreak{}compiler/\allowbreak{}src/\allowbreak{}Frontend/\allowbreak{}Lift.\allowbreak{}elm}), and the host effect loop
(\texttt{src/\allowbreak{}effectloop.\allowbreak{}zig}); the research extension itself --- the
branch-local refinement machinery in \texttt{Type/\allowbreak{}Unify.\allowbreak{}elm} and
\texttt{Type/\allowbreak{}Infer.\allowbreak{}elm}, with its surface (the \texttt{type\ a.}
binders, exhaustiveness and refutation checking); the Lean mechanization
(\texttt{lean/\allowbreak{}}); the verification harness --- the artifact's
verification script, the fixture gate
(\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}fixtures/\allowbreak{}run-\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}gate.\allowbreak{}sh}), the corpus baseline (the
committed corpus manifest), and the recount script; the adversarial test
passes --- the three-pass unsound-accept hunt and the fixtures pinning
its findings; and the artifact packaging --- \texttt{ARTIFACT.\allowbreak{}md}, the
generated fixture matrix (\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}elm-\allowbreak{}fixtures/\allowbreak{}MATRIX.\allowbreak{}md}), and
the prerequisite preflights. The compiler substrate is
\emph{pre-existing} in §6's sense --- it predates the contribution ---
but it was built inside this project's sessions, with the same
assistance.

\textbf{The degree, as the record shows it.} Every commit in this
repository's history carries the author's name
(\texttt{git\ log\ -\allowbreak{}\/\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}format=\textquotesingle{}\%an\textquotesingle{}\ \textbar{}\ sort\ \textbar{}\ uniq\ -\allowbreak{}c}
prints the author's name and nothing else). The commit record alone
therefore says nothing about the assistance: it credits the author for
work that the project's working records show was written by AI coding
agents --- several underlying models, dispatched per work unit --- with
the author directing and committing the results, and two early commits
in the parent repository from which this one was split carry the coding
agents' own sandbox identity. The record does not support a per-line or
per-component percentage. Parts of the artifact are \emph{ports of
third-party code}, not original code by anyone --- the vendored
elm-syntax parser (from the Elm compiler), the vendored native runtime
(descended from a Zig port of the Shen ZINC VM), and the elm/\allowbreak{}core
libraries; there, the assistance was in the porting and adaptation.

\textbf{The human role.} The author directed the work, made the design
decisions (the discipline itself, the naming, the scope, and what not to
claim), constructed the motivating example, and independently
re-verified the headline numbers before they were printed here. No AI
system is an author: under the ACM policy, generative AI tools cannot be
listed as authors under any conditions, and the author is accountable
for the content regardless of its source. The deposit-side note states
the same facts for a reader who arrives at the code first
(\texttt{ARTIFACT.\allowbreak{}md} §8).

For completeness, the non-required half: drafting and review of this
paper's prose were also AI-assisted. The policy does not require that to
be disclosed; it is stated here because the boundary between the two
halves is this project's actual history. ---

\section{7 Related work, organized by the feature-pair
map}\label{related-work-organized-by-the-feature-pair-map}

The organization of this section is itself a contribution. Three
features --- \textbf{R} row polymorphism, \textbf{G} GADT refinement,
\textbf{A} explicit/\allowbreak{}locally abstract polymorphism --- pick out cells by
the pairs they combine, and the map (26 rows --- 24 retrieved from
primary sources, 2 carried second-hand; the survey with verbatim quotes
and URLs is the companion survey) makes two things visible at once:
\emph{which adjacent cells are occupied} --- so that ``but X did rows''
and ``but Y did GADTs'' are answered before they are asked --- and
\emph{that one specific cell is empty}. No published type system refines
a row variable by a branch-local GADT equation, and no published system
therefore says which record operations remain typable when such an
equation is active. (The nearest sounding sentence in the literature ---
CORELINKS' ``our case construct refines variant types'' --- is examined
in §7.2: presence flip, variant row, no equation.) The claim is about
published systems with a \emph{designed discipline}; it is never worded
``rows and GADTs have never been combined'' --- OCaml ships the raw
combination as an idiom, and its boundary is discovered empirically by
its users.

The claim is falsifiable, and the survey that backs it states the
method. Every row of the map is a published system --- 24 of the 26
retrieved from a primary source (paper, language documentation, or
maintainer record), 2 carried second-hand --- and classified by the
feature pairs it ships; the survey records the query terms run and a
would-be-breakers table giving each candidate examined and why it falls
short of the cell. A referee who knows a published system with a
\emph{designed discipline} that refines a row variable by a branch-local
GADT equation is asked to name it: one such system occupies the cell and
refutes the claim. The rows-only side of the map carries the method's
clearest positive control: PureScript ships row-polymorphic records and
its core team has argued GADTs out --- ``I think we should commit to not
adding GADTs'' (hdgarrood, 2019) --- so the pair cannot arise there by
first-party decision rather than by oversight.

\subsection{7.1 The rows-only lineage
(R)}\label{the-rows-only-lineage-r}

\textbf{Wand 1989} types record \emph{concatenation} and loses
principality for it --- ``this calculus does not have principal types,
but does have finite complete sets of types'' --- compensating with
finite complete sets. Our fragment Q loses principality for a different
trigger (refinement-with-mentioning-result, not concatenation):
\textbf{the same casualty, a different mechanism --- we do not conflate
the two}, and Wand's compensation suggests a question for future work
(does Q admit finite complete sets?). \textbf{Rémy 1994} is the
reference point for the operation dial: unrestricted extension
unconditionally (\texttt{new\_\allowbreak{}a}), presence flags as quantification
(System Π*), and update-as-extension --- the expressiveness maximum our
conditional insertion rejection trades against (Section 3.3).
\textbf{Gaster \& Jones 1996} dial extension to strict under a lacks
predicate and type update as restrict-then-extend --- the second
published position on the dial. \textbf{Ohori 1995} replaces row
variables with \emph{kind restrictions} on instantiation --- worth
citing against our kinding findings (Section 6.1): the kinds are
load-bearing, but without a row variable there is nothing to refine ---
the seat itself is absent. \textbf{Leijen 2005} is the substrate: scoped
labels, the eq-swap rewrite, and the duplicate-label semantics our H1
commutation is stated over; the paper predates GADT inference and
contains no occurrence of refinement. \textbf{Paszke \& Xie 2023, Spanò
2024, Hubers et al.~2025} extend the R lineage (infix extension for
tabular data, overloading conversion, row-typed recursion) with zero
GADT content --- grep-measured on the retrieved texts. \textbf{Toohey,
Chen, Jamalzadeh \& Xie 2026} occupies the adjacent \textbf{rows ×
type-classes} cell, not the R lineage: dictionary-passing elaboration of
ad-hoc polymorphism over polymorphic rows, with \texttt{All} (a property
across all fields), \texttt{ind} (a fold over rows),
\texttt{Split}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{Lift}, and commutativity annotations over a
\emph{parameterised} row theory, all mechanized in Lean 4 --- and the
grep on its 38-page full text is \texttt{GADT} 0, \texttt{refine} 0,
\texttt{refinement} 0, \texttt{branch} 0: no equations on rows, so its
delta from us is exactly the refinement interaction. That cell is
\textbf{out of scope} here: we claim nothing about rows × type classes,
and generic structural dispatch over rows is their result (\texttt{All}
+ \texttt{ind}), not a consequence of our discipline.

\subsection{7.2 Presence: the nearest neighbour in one
dimension}\label{presence-the-nearest-neighbour-in-one-dimension}

\textbf{CORELINKS} {[}Lindley \& Cheney 2012{]} is the closest published
system to answering ``what must an operation know about which fields are
present?'': it types insert/\allowbreak{}update/\allowbreak{}delete against
\texttt{(label\ ×\ presence\ ×\ type)} rows by \emph{quantifying} a
presence variable over the needed row --- ``presence \ldots{} is
unconstrained as we can infer nothing about it solely from an insert or
update operation''. This is \textbf{abstraction} --- the opposite
direction from our \emph{assumption} on a rigid variable inside a branch
--- and it has no equations, no rigidity, and no branch-local store. Its
rows also have \textbf{distinct labels}, which is precisely the case
where our domain rule is \emph{exact} (Section 4.4): the duplicate-label
coarseness is a genuine expressiveness difference between the systems,
in both directions. One sentence in CORELINKS sounds close to our cell:
``our case construct refines variant types, whereas OCaml's equivalent
does not'' (its §2.1). What that case construct does is flip a
\textbf{presence flag} --- the CASE rule refines ``the type of the value
being matched'' so that ``the non-matched label is absent'' in the type
of the variable bound by the default branch --- and it does so on a
\textbf{variant} row, adopting no equation: the words \texttt{GADT},
\texttt{rigid}, \texttt{skolem}, and \texttt{equation} never occur in
the paper (grep-measured). Our cell is none of these: a branch-local
equation \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{\ ℓ\ :\ t\ \textbar{}\ ρ\textquotesingle{}\ \}}
on a record's row variable. \textbf{Castagna \& Peyrot 2025} give
presence polymorphism over optional fields in a set-theoretic system and
bracket refinement explicitly: ``type cases, guards, or type narrowing
\ldots{} seem mostly orthogonal to the introduction of row
polymorphism'' --- the live assumption our cell falsifies for the
product half.

\subsection{7.3 The GADT-inference lineage
(G)}\label{the-gadt-inference-lineage-g}

\textbf{OutsideIn(X)} {[}Vytiniotis et al.~2011{]} is the standard
baseline: implication constraints with \emph{touchables} --- variables
the solver may unify inside a given constraint. It cannot state our
problem: its type grammar
\texttt{τ\ ::=\ tv\ \textbar{}\ Int\ \textbar{}\ Bool\ \textbar{}\ {[}τ{]}\ \textbar{}\ T\ τ}
has no record type, no row variable, no presence (grep-measured).
\textbf{Stratified inference} {[}Pottier \& Régis-Gianas 2006{]}
introduces type equations at case constructs and propagates them through
annotations --- the annotation-meaning caveat we share (``moving a type
annotation into or out of a case construct can change its meaning''),
with rows never appearing as types. \textbf{Wobbly types} {[}Peyton
Jones et al.~2006{]} put rigidity in the environment per annotation; the
word ``row'' does not occur in the paper. \textbf{Ambivalent types}
{[}Garrigue \& Rémy 2013{]} formalize OCaml's locally abstract types ---
a rigid variable ``can be refined by GADT pattern matching'' --- with
scoped equations that may not leak out of a branch: the closest
\emph{mechanism} to ours, on a grammar
(\texttt{τ\ ::=\ α\ \textbar{}\ a\ \textbar{}\ τ→τ\ \textbar{}\ eq(τ,τ)\ \textbar{}\ int})
that cannot state \texttt{ρ\ ≐\ \{l:t\textbar{}ρ\textquotesingle{}\}}.
\textbf{Choice types} {[}Chen \& Erwig 2016{]} are the nearest G-lineage
neighbour to our boundary: they carry branch refinements \emph{in the
type language} --- choice types \texttt{D⟨φ̄⟩}, alternatives synchronised
by name, with a separate reconciliation phase that replaces choices by
type index variables --- and price it in their own words, ``principality
comes at the price of having choice types in the type language''. Their
grammar (\texttt{τ\ ::=\ α\ \textbar{}\ τ→τ\ \textbar{}\ T\ τ}) has no
record type, no row variable, and no presence (grep-measured on the
retrieved text): refinement reaches only GADT type-constructor
parameters, never a row --- they stop at the boundary this paper
crosses.

\textbf{HMG(X) {[}Simonet \& Pottier 2007{]} is the un-walked door.} It
is a parameterised, constraint-based account of guarded ADTs --- every
branch checked ``under different assumptions about the type variables in
scope'' --- that could in principle host a row theory: X is a parameter.
But no published instantiation of it (or of OutsideIn's X) targets a
row/\allowbreak{}record theory --- the only Rémy citation in HMG(X) is the
\emph{object} calculus --- and the two row-specific obligations our
discipline needs, H1's commutation under scoped-label
\textbf{duplicates} and the \textbf{domain} escape rule, do not come out
of the generic frame for free. λρG is that instantiation, with the two
obligations carried explicitly (Section 4). This is the strongest
positioning sentence available: we claim the instantiation and the two
row obligations, not a new frame.

\subsection{7.4 The combination cell and its
occupants}\label{the-combination-cell-and-its-occupants}

\textbf{OCaml} is the one widely used system with all three features,
and its record is the paper's strongest single piece of prior-art
evidence: restricted in the first implementation (Garrigue \& Rémy 2012,
verbatim, on the same row-variable invariant our discipline protects),
still ``not well specified'' per its maintainers (octachron 2024), with
poly-variant patterns blocking refinement outright (``GADT equations
cannot narrow a polymorphic variant constraint'' {[}octachron 2024{]};
the earlier, stronger 4.00-era restriction --- ``types cannot be refined
if a pattern-matching contains polymorphic variant'' --- was lifted in
4.01 {[}Garrigue, \#5724 rev 13221; 4.01 Changes{]}), object/\allowbreak{}GADT
invariance (``GADTs are incompatible with object subtyping: they are
always invariant with respect to their type parameters''), and the
recommended workaround --- one row variable per field --- being a manual
membership-witness encoding, the idiom practitioners already reach for
(the discuss.ocaml.org FSM/\allowbreak{}reducer threads are the user-demand
datapoints, and Section 1.4's program is one of them, translated).
\textbf{Flix} restrictable variants {[}Madsen et al.~2023{]} refine a
\emph{label-set} index under \texttt{choose} while the record row index
is only ever extended --- refinement never flows into the row --- and
name GADTs as ``interesting future work''. \textbf{GHC's
\texttt{Has\allowbreak{}Field}} on record GADTs is class-triggered unification over
\emph{nominal} records --- no row variables. \textbf{Koka} uses rows for
effects with duplicate labels inherited from Leijen, and its
eliminations \emph{unify} the effect row (\texttt{catch} unifies μ with
\texttt{(exn\textbar{}μ\textquotesingle{})}) --- never refine it; we
cite it for the effect half of the duality and claim nothing about
rows-and-effects.

\subsection{7.5 The frontier}\label{the-frontier}

\textbf{Omnidirectional inference} {[}O'Brien, Rémy \& Scherer 2026{]}
restores principality for fragile features (record-label overloading;
semi-explicit polymorphism) by reordering constraint solving --- and
names GADTs as the application they ``would be interested in studying'',
over \emph{nominal} records. The field is actively rebuilding inference
around the principality casualty our boundary measures; our result lands
the row-side answer next to it. \textbf{Fan, Xu \& Xie 2025} implement
touchability as \emph{levels} in production checkers --- useful
vocabulary for the implementability of R (our rigid set) --- with GADTs
explicitly deferred.


\section{8 Limitations}\label{limitations}

We state the limitations as first-class results, not as apology: several
of them are theorem- or fixture-backed boundaries (marked), and none is
silently hedged.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{No general soundness theorem} \emph{(paper-gap: the wording is
  the fix)}. Progress and preservation are argued, not proved. The
  mechanization's 90 theorems --- over 3 axiom parameters --- are
  typing-judgment theorems: the row algebra, the store discipline, the
  escape rule, the update theorem, and record-operation preservation,
  conditional on the unifier abstracted as a parameter. What they carry
  are exactly the two row-specific obligations the argued soundness
  rests on; the whole judgment is not covered. Later revisions must not
  upgrade ``argued'' to ``proved''.
\item
  \textbf{The escape check is sound but over-approximate --- proved, not
  hedged} (\texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}overapproximation}): it rejects some legitimate
  returns. The duplicate-label case is \emph{coarse} --- proved
  (\texttt{h2b\_\allowbreak{}domain\_\allowbreak{}exactness}: exact for fresh labels, coarse for
  duplicates) --- and its false reject is pinned by a do-not-weaken
  fixture (\texttt{rowgadt\_\allowbreak{}dup\_\allowbreak{}fewer}). ``Fixing'' it by weakening the
  check would reintroduce the unsoundness class the hunt closed.
\item
  \textbf{Fragment Q is checkable, not inferable.} Signatureless native
  row-GADT code with a result-mentioning refinement is rejected; the
  signature is not optional there (Section 5). The retry path is
  additionally incomplete: a GADT case nested under a \texttt{let} is
  spuriously rejected (\texttt{g\allowbreak{}Neg\_\allowbreak{}letcase}) --- soundness-neutral,
  and no completeness claim is made.
\item
  \textbf{Refutation is conditional.} Exhaustiveness and refutation
  checking exists and is pinned (\texttt{adtgaps}, \texttt{refutpos},
  \texttt{refutneg}, \texttt{refutbare}), but refutation fires only
  where the scrutinee's index is \textbf{concrete or binder-rigid}; a
  bare flexible index never licenses refuting a sibling (that condition
  is itself pinned by \texttt{refutbare}, after the check initially
  accepted a partial function through a flexible index --- found and
  fixed during the work). GADT-ness is classified per file, so a
  hypothetical cross-module GADT index degrades to the old flexible
  behaviour (safe, via the too-general police and the refutation guard;
  unexercised by the corpus). One pre-existing false positive for
  unsignatured nested patterns remains.
\item
  \textbf{Per-file kinding} \emph{(stated as an approximation)}. ADT
  generic kinds are collected per file, so a cross-file bare row
  parameter could kind as a type variable --- a soundness-relevant
  approximation, unexercised by the corpus and fixtures. The declarative
  spec states kinds; the elaboration is a front-end concern.
\item
  \textbf{Rank-2 /\allowbreak{} higher-rank types are absent} --- the type
  representation has no quantifier node, so the general handler
  signature (a polymorphic continuation) cannot be stated. Deliberate:
  orthogonal to the row×GADT claim, and landing it would move the
  evidence baseline under the paper.
\item
  \textbf{Surface gaps} \emph{(all completeness, not soundness)}: no
  type-level strings (labels are surface strings;
  \texttt{Has\ "x"\ t\ ρ} is inexpressible, so the example fixes
  \texttt{l} by the record's signature instead); record literals are
  closed (an open row can only be \emph{named}, never constructed);
  \texttt{\{\ \textbar{}\ ρ\ \}} bare-open does not parse; the update
  base must be a local variable.
\item
  \textbf{The membership-witness reducer is definable but not callable
  at a concrete witness} ---
  \texttt{read\ Here\ \{\ n\ =\ 1,\ closed\ =\ 2\ \}} errs
  \texttt{cannot\ unify\ a\ with\ \{l:a\textbar{}\ b\}}, the global
  bare-\texttt{KRow}-variable-vs-record gap outside branch mode (Section
  1.4); the FSM example keeps the witness as a shape, not a working
  reducer. Relatedly, argument order matters for the FSM reducers
  (record-first checks; the symmetric event-first form is rejected at
  its call site) --- an inference-order artifact of the implementation,
  which we report and do not attribute to typing-rule bias.
\item
  \textbf{The trusted-body residue is a representation problem} --- the
  interpreter's holdout is a dynamic cast at the VM boundary
  (\texttt{a\ ≐\ List\ a}), and the remaining trusted bodies decompose
  into lies of representation, not of refinement (Section 6.4): the
  honest fix is a surface change or an honest datatype, not more type
  theory.
\item
  \textbf{Evaluation is self-corpus plus designed fixtures} ---
  byte-identity is the \emph{non-regression} evidence, not a benchmark
  claim, and we claim no user-facing benefit; we claim a characterized
  boundary. The one external program (Section 1.4) is a translation with
  three stated boundaries, not a corpus study. The adversarial hunt was
  three passes: five unsound accepts found and fixed (two in the first
  escape check, two in the shipping checks, one in the coercion surface,
  the last closed by a class-level repair), and one runnability bug the
  gate could not see; absence of more is evidence, not proof. No
  performance numbers are claimed (the retry fires only on the failure
  path).
\end{itemize}


\section{9 Conclusion}\label{conclusion}

The conflict between row polymorphism and GADT refinement is an artifact
of eager global solving, not of the features: a row variable under a
branch-local equation is coherent, useful, and \emph{characterizable}
once the equation is captured rather than solved, type equations are
discharged at results while row equations never are, and the
discipline's costs are located --- principality in exactly the fragment
that refines a signature variable through two sibling branches,
expressiveness in the insertion the discipline must reject. The
discipline is implemented, measured against a byte-identical corpus,
mechanized where it is load-bearing, and falsifiable where it is not:
the fixtures that pin its boundary are the artifact's regression gate.
What remains open --- general soundness, the refutation condition's
generalization, the restrictable-variant dual (the calculus is phrased
so the dual statement is a polarity flip), and whether fragment Q admits
Wand-style finite complete sets --- is stated, not hidden.

\texttt{Typing\allowbreak{}Store.\allowbreak{}lean} & 29 & store lemmas: weakening, monotonicity,
the R-LET refined-tail exclusions, \texttt{tier\_\allowbreak{}R\_\allowbreak{}forces\_\allowbreak{}escape},
\texttt{refined\allowbreak{}Tail\allowbreak{}Var\_\allowbreak{}iff\_\allowbreak{}insertion\allowbreak{}Rejected} \\
\texttt{Preserve.\allowbreak{}lean} & 18 & record-operation preservation (Section
4.6): \texttt{sel}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{sel\allowbreak{}Disch}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{upd} preserves, the
two-tier soundness, the first-occurrence correspondence;
\texttt{unifies\_\allowbreak{}field\_\allowbreak{}projection} as the third axiom parameter \\
\end{longtable}
}

The three axioms are parameters, not gaps in proofs:
\texttt{Unifies}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{Captures} are the unifier as a parameter of the
theory (Section 4.1), and \texttt{unifies\_\allowbreak{}field\_\allowbreak{}projection} is the one
property the plain-selection preservation case needs of the abstract
unifier. Every other theorem closes against the local Lean binary with
no sorry.

\subsection{Appendix A correction (2026-10-10, evidence-chain
re-aim)}\label{appendix-a-correction-2026-10-10-evidence-chain-re-aim}

\textbf{SUPERSEDED IN FULL by the 2026-10-11 correction below.} This
correction was measured while the ZINC interpreter still existed: its
\texttt{PASS=268}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{PASS=156} counts, its
\texttt{ELM\_\allowbreak{}GATE\_\allowbreak{}NATIVE} switch and its two ``single-engine for now''
rows (\texttt{rawrun}, \texttt{depth}) all describe a tree that was
deleted at P8. It is kept as the record of what was true on 2026-10-10
and must not be read as a statement about the current tree.

\emph{Appended, not reworded --- the paragraph above still describes the
tree it was measured on. Correction:} as of this date the fixture gate
no longer runs its executable rows through the ZINC VM alone. Every
\texttt{run} /\allowbreak{} \texttt{run2} /\allowbreak{} \texttt{io} /\allowbreak{} \texttt{sigdeath} row (112
rows) now has a \textbf{native twin}: the same sources are compiled
through the QBE backend (elm → \texttt{.\allowbreak{}ssa} → vendored qbe → cc +
\texttt{rt.\allowbreak{}o}) and the native binary must print the \emph{same pinned
expected output} the VM row asserts (\texttt{PASS=268\ FAIL=0} at the
tip; \texttt{ELM\_\allowbreak{}GATE\_\allowbreak{}NATIVE=0} reproduces the VM-only gate verbatim,
\texttt{PASS=156\ FAIL=0}). The \texttt{run} rows above therefore hold
on \textbf{both} engines. Two rows remain single-engine by construction
and are stated as losses, not hidden: \texttt{rawrun} (a hand-written
csexp bundle no Elm source can produce) has no native twin and dies with
the bundle format; \texttt{depth} asserts the interpreter's
\texttt{CALL\_\allowbreak{}STACK\_\allowbreak{}DEPTH} cap and its native counterpart is the
separate \texttt{natdepth} row. The VM-vs-native \textbf{differential}
that motivated this appendix's trust story --- two backends agreeing
byte-for-byte on the same input --- is being retired with the ZINC
backend; its replacements (golden outputs harvested from the VM's last
verified run, a frozen \texttt{.\allowbreak{}ssa} corpus baseline, GC-churn reruns,
structural counters, and the whole-compiler \texttt{.\allowbreak{}ssa} fixed point)
are a \textbf{regression net, not a differential}: a wrong-but-plausible
output on an unpinned shape is no longer caught by construction. The
planned Lua backend would restore a true differential (two backends, two
value representations, Lua's own GC). See \texttt{ARTIFACT.\allowbreak{}md} §9 for
the full statement.


\subsection{Appendix A correction (2026-10-11, P8: the ZINC interpreter
is
gone)}\label{appendix-a-correction-2026-10-11-p8-the-zinc-interpreter-is-gone}

\textbf{This correction SUPERSEDES the whole of the 2026-10-10
correction above.} That one was measured while the ZINC interpreter
still existed; it is kept here, figures and all, as the record of what
was true on 2026-10-10, and nothing in it states anything about the
current tree. What follows is measured on the tip \emph{after} the
deletion.

\textbf{What left the tree.} The interpreter package
\texttt{vendor/\allowbreak{}zinc-\allowbreak{}vm}, everything that linked it (the \texttt{elmvm}
driver, the benchmark driver, \texttt{tools/\allowbreak{}aot/\allowbreak{}}, the self-host compile
and gate scripts), the csexp backend (\texttt{Zinc/\allowbreak{}Emit.\allowbreak{}elm},
\texttt{Zinc/\allowbreak{}Csexp.\allowbreak{}elm}, \texttt{Mid/\allowbreak{}To\allowbreak{}Zinc.\allowbreak{}elm} and the ZINC-only
mid-tier passes), the \texttt{MIDTIER=0}-vs-\texttt{1} differential and
its tooling, and the committed csexp bootstrap seed. What stays is what
the earlier correction already named as the replacement: the frontend,
the checker, the Lean mechanization, the vendored native runtime, and
the QBE backend the fixtures now execute through.

\textbf{The execution model is native, and only native.} The gate's
executable rows (\texttt{run}, \texttt{run2}, \texttt{run\_\allowbreak{}io},
\texttt{sigdeath} --- 112 rows) compile the fixture through the QBE
backend (elm → \texttt{.\allowbreak{}ssa} → the vendored qbe → cc + \texttt{rt.\allowbreak{}o})
and run the resulting binary. There is no interpreter in the tree and no
interpreter-only mode, so the previous correction's claim that the
\texttt{run} rows hold on both engines no longer has a second engine
behind it: the rows hold, and the bytes they are held against are the
\emph{same pinned \texttt{expected/\allowbreak{}*.\allowbreak{}txt} files}, but the sentence that
said they execute \emph{through the VM} is false and has been corrected
in place in Appendix A rather than reworded here.

\textbf{The counts at the tip.} Gate \texttt{PASS=154\ FAIL=0}. Corpus
byte-identity 149 = 149 against the \texttt{.\allowbreak{}ssa} anchor.
\texttt{Test\allowbreak{}Main} 95 assertions. The native slice runner
\texttt{tools/\allowbreak{}qbe/\allowbreak{}qbe-\allowbreak{}check.\allowbreak{}sh} 221 PASS /\allowbreak{} 0 FAIL (104 committed goldens
plus the cross-target rows). The whole-compiler \texttt{.\allowbreak{}ssa} fixed
point byte-identical. Seed status
\texttt{none\ —\ retired\ at\ P8,\ pending\ the\ Lua\ backend}. The
environment switch the previous correction's recipe used,
\texttt{ELM\_\allowbreak{}GATE\_\allowbreak{}NATIVE}, no longer exists, so that recipe cannot be
run at all.

\textbf{The two rows the previous correction named as its single-engine
losses are themselves gone.} \texttt{rawrun} (a hand-written csexp
bundle no Elm source can produce) died with the format, and
\texttt{depth} (which asserted the interpreter's call-stack cap) died
with the interpreter; its native counterpart \texttt{natdepth} stays,
and is registered.

\textbf{The paper's own figures, corrected in the body.} The
load-bearing numbers this deletion moved were corrected where they are
claimed, not only in this appendix --- the counts, the execution-method
sentence, and the reproducibility claim:

The \texttt{necessary}/\allowbreak{}\texttt{sufficient} argument's decomposition
moved with the total: the gate registers 154 checks, of which 29 are the
frontend lambda-lift fixtures (\texttt{MATRIX.\allowbreak{}md} rows 125--153, the
\texttt{lift*} names); the third category that decomposition named, a
hand-crafted-bundle run, is gone with the csexp format.

\textbf{What did not change.} The differential loss the previous
correction states stands, and stands unmitigated: there is one backend,
so a same-input backend disagreement on a shape no fixture pins is
invisible. The anchors that replaced it --- golden outputs, the
\texttt{.\allowbreak{}ssa} corpus baseline, the GC-churn reruns, the structural
counters, the whole-compiler \texttt{.\allowbreak{}ssa} fixed point --- are a
\textbf{regression net, not a differential}. \texttt{ARTIFACT.\allowbreak{}md}
sections 9.5 and 9.6 carry the full statement, including what a golden
can and cannot be evidence for now that it has no second implementation
to agree with.
